title: The signature sheet restates nothing

title: Every piece detail fails and traps the user
observation: Every product tap in every lane returns "Couldn't load product" / "Let's try that again". Retry fails identically, the edge-swipe back does nothing, and `scan_ui` returns exactly one element for the whole screen — the retry link. The only escape is force-quitting the app. Root cause: `GET /rest/v1/products?id=eq.…&select=*,vendors(name,made_in,brand_story)` returns HTTP 300 `PGRST201`, because `products` carries two foreign keys to `vendors`.
why_it_matters: The screen where a buyer reads the maker's story and the price is unreachable, and reaching for it destroys a guest's whole session.
already_ruled: C27 — named as genuinely app-side and fair game | C27 names this as genuinely app-side, distinct from the local edge-function 503s | C27 names this explicitly as app-side and fair game (distinct from the local edge-function 503s) | C19 (screen-chrome exemption is deliberate for the success state; this finding is about the error state having no exit of its own, not about the exemption itself)
proposal_seeds: Qualify the ambiguous embed as vendors!products_vendor_id_fkey(...) and give the error state a Back control.
Qualify the embed as vendors!products_vendor_id_fkey(...) at ProductAPIClient.swift:99.
Disambiguate the embed to vendors!products_vendor_id_fkey(...) and give the error state a Back control.

title: Push never fires for proposals, invoices or decisions

Zero push callers touch invoices, proposals, decisions or direct_orders; notification-dispatch accepts channel "push" and writes a log row instead.
why_it_matters: A designer sending a proposal or raising an invoice has no way to reach the client's phone, so the app is not the channel and the designer keeps sending emails.

title: The engaged home is the guest home
observation: For an account whose design-request lead was accepted and claimed on Aug 18, and which already uploaded a room scan, the home reads "NEXT MOVE / Bring your first room into Patina / A short scan gives the Companion a real space to work from." title: Buying ends at "Add to Room / Saved ✓"

observation: The card ⋯ menu offers only "Save", "Share", "Not for me", "View details" — no "Add to room" — including when the grid is entered from the room's own "Browse Picks for This Room" button, which opens the same unfiltered "10 pieces curated for your space" with no room name. title: Two weeks away looks like one hour away
observation: A relaunch drops the signed-in client on a byte-identical "Today": no welcome-back, no unread marker, no last-visit timestamp, no activity feed. No last-seen timestamp exists for the feed, the story, the room or the saved list anywhere in the app; ContextMemoryStore records only a coarse activity kind and is off until the user turns it on. Two silent time-based changes are never explained: a matched request card disappears on day fifteen, and the Companion graduates to its calm state at fourteen days.
why_it_matters: An app that cannot say what happened while you were gone has no memory of you, and a home-furnishing project is measured in weeks, not sessions.
already_ruled: C23 — Option B's Today contract permits a truthful fallback, which is what a "nothing new" line would be
proposal_seeds: Record a last-opened timestamp and render one honest line above Today: what moved, or that nothing did.
Store a last-opened timestamp and render one dated "since you were here" line above the Next Move.

title: Dimensions and lead time exist nowhere
observation: The piece surface carries maker, name, materials as a joined subtitle, price, an "{n}% match" pill, provenance chips and a maker story. It carries no dimensions, no lead time, no stock, no shipping, no returns policy, no description and no link to the maker's own page. `products.dimensions JSONB` exists in the schema and is neither returned by `get_recommendations` nor decoded by the app.
why_it_matters: Nobody buys a four-thousand-dollar chair without knowing whether it fits through the door or when it arrives; two of the five fields a purchase needs are in the database and simply never sent.
proposal_seeds: Return products.dimensions from get_recommendations, decode it, and print it under the price as "W × D × H".
Widen `get_recommendations` and the product fetch to return dimensions and lead_time_weeks, and render them under the price.

title: 18 × 14 ft is stored as 59' × 46'
observation: With the toggle reading "ft", LENGTH 18 and WIDTH 14 were typed; the next screen — "YOUR SPACE / Here's what I see." — returned a room of "46 ft" × "59 ft" and "2713 SQUARE FEET", and those figures persist into the room view ("Living Room / 2713 SQ FT · 2 WINDOWS", "59' × 46'"), Your Spaces, and the home's ACTIVE ROOM card.
why_it_matters: The app silently multiplies the one measurement a downsizer cares about by 3.28 and then presents it back as fact — after which no number it shows can be believed.
proposal_seeds: Stop converting a value the reader entered in the displayed unit, and make ft/m a 44-point segmented control with a visible selected state.
Apply the metre-to-foot conversion only when the unit toggle is actually on "m", and echo the entered unit on the summary.

title: No order object anywhere in the client app
observation: "Where is it?" resolves only to project, proposal, invoice and decision state. The project detail is three stats ("BUDGET $120,000", "STATUS In Progress", "CLIENT VIEW Milestone"), an "Invoices / View and pay your invoices" row and a portal link — no items, no orders, no deliveries, no dates.
why_it_matters: Post-purchase tracking is the strongest honest reason to reopen a furnishing app, and there is nothing in the client for it to show.
already_ruled: C24 (direct_orders status vocabulary is only pending_payment/paid/canceled)

title: Portal instruction for me rendered to my client
observation: The client's own project screen carries a boxed line reading "Set up phases, payments, and FF&E in the portal →" — an instruction written for the designer, displayed to the homeowner. It is a StaticText, not a button, so it looks tappable and is not.
why_it_matters: The client is reading the designer's back-office to-do list on their own project, which reads as sloppiness the designer will be blamed for and undermines trust in the money screens next to it.
proposal_seeds: Replace the missing-section portal link with client-facing copy naming what is not ready yet, and never render a portal instruction on a client surface.

title: No way to message the designer from anywhere
observation: The entire messaging surface is a Studio block reading "Conversation 0" and "No project conversations yet." There is no compose field, no thread list, no "message your designer" affordance anywhere in the signed-in app, on any screen.
why_it_matters: A client sitting on an overdue decision, an unpaid invoice and an expiring proposal has no in-app way to ask a single question, so every hesitation becomes a text to the designer's phone.
proposal_seeds: Give the Conversation block a first-message composer that opens a thread when none exists.

title: A direct order would credit the designer nothing
observation: public.direct_orders carries id, client_id, product_id, product_name, quantity, unit_price_cents, amount_cents, currency, status, stripe ids, shipping, created_at, paid_at — and no designer_id, no project_id, no commission_rate and no FF&E link. The platform's own migration states it: "No designer attribution (client_id is the buyer)". The earnings ledger credits from invoice_payments only.
why_it_matters: The day a Buy now button ships on the client, a designer's specified piece can be bought at retail inside the app the designer sent the client to, with no margin, no schedule line and no notice — which ends the designer's willingness to refer clients.
already_ruled: C11/C24 — the rail is ratified backlog and the attribution decision is explicitly still open
proposal_seeds: Add designer_id, project_id and a commission_rate snapshot to direct_orders before the client-side buy button exists, not after.

title: Guest's room and taste portrait adopted by the account
observation: After a guest session, client@patina.dev — an account with zero rooms and zero saved items server-side — shows "ACTIVE ROOM / Living Room" on Today, "1 ROOM" and "1 SAVED PIECE" in the Companion, and "✦ Modern Warmth / 1 ROOMS / 1 SAVED" on Profile. Your Spaces flags the same room "SAVED ON THIS PHONE" while every other surface counts it as account data. It cleared only when the local store was wiped.
why_it_matters: One household member's rooms and taste profile silently become another's, and a designer's client sees a home that is not theirs on the first screen after sign-in.
already_ruled: C27 — named as genuinely app-side and fair game
proposal_seeds: Scope the SwiftData store to the signed-in user id and offer an explicit "claim your guest saves" step at sign-in.

title: "Get design help" from an already-matched client files an indistinguishable second lead
observation: For the engaged account (a lead accepted 8 days ago per the seed), 'Studio → Get design help' opens 'Your design request / No scans on this phone yet / You can scan a room to attach — or request design help without one below', with 'Request without a scan' as the only act — a brand-new lead-intake form, not a status view or a message to the existing designer.
why_it_matters: A client who taps the app's own designer-help control after we've already matched has no way to know it's about to file a second, unlinked request into my (or someone else's) intake queue — exactly the kind of duplicate that costs me time to untangle.
proposal_seeds: Branch design-request submission on an existing accepted lead and route to 'Message your designer' instead of a new intake form.

title: Engaged client's home/Companion show zero trace of the accepted designer
observation: The engaged account's home Next Move reads "Bring your first room into Patina / A short scan gives the Companion a real space to work from" — byte-identical to the guest/discovering pitch — and the Companion panel offers "Add your first space / Retake the quiz / Your recommendations / Your profile" with no "Your studio" row at all, for a homeowner whose lead was accepted 8 days ago and who already uploaded a scan.
why_it_matters: The single true fact about this client's account — that a designer accepted them — appears nowhere in the product; if that's what my client sees after we match, they have every reason to wonder whether the match actually happened.
proposal_seeds: Surface the matched designer's name and a status card on the engaged home instead of the discovering-tier pitch.

title: Buy-now backend built with zero designer attribution
observation: public.direct_orders (00276_direct_orders.sql) is a complete, wired buy-now rail — create_direct_order RPC, create-checkout-session dispatch, stripe-webhook settle branch, receipt emails — with columns id, client_id, product_id, product_name, quantity, unit_price_cents, amount_cents, status, stripe ids, shipping. No designer_id, no project_id, no commission_rate. 00301_marketplace_vitals.sql states outright: "No designer attribution (client_id is the buyer)." Zero iOS client code references it.
why_it_matters: This is the answer to my own question: if this ships as-is, a client can buy the same piece I sourced directly through Patina, I get zero commission, it never lands on my FF&E schedule, and I find out only when something goes wrong with the delivery — the exact scenario I've already been burned by once, now built into the platform I recommend to clients.
proposal_seeds: Add designer_id/project_id/commission_rate to direct_orders and an earnings-credit branch before any iOS buy-now surface ships.

title: Auth wall lands at the last tap, no escape
observation: After four screens of the design-request flow, "Send request" throws the full gate — "PATINA / Welcome home / Start with a piece you love" — as a sheet with no Cancel, no ✕ and no "Look around first"; the same sheet reached from the sign-in path does have a Cancel. Nothing in the flow said an account would be needed.
why_it_matters: The moment a guest has typed their budget and their hopes is the moment they judge whether the company is careful, and the app takes their escape hatches away.
already_ruled: C9 — the auth sheet presents over context and never ejects; that half holds, but this variant ships with no dismiss control
july_status: residual — U21's Studio-row entry variant of the same AuthSheet plumbing was never exercised in the July passes
proposal_seeds: Say "you'll sign in to send this" on the first step of the flow, and give the sheet a Cancel.

title: A returning guest is dumped at "Welcome home"
observation: After a relaunch the guest lands on the gate reading "Welcome home" / "Start with a piece you love" with the session, the quiz progress and the room gone; the saved piece and the coach-mark flags do survive, and Profile still shows the "Warm Modern" badge while the Companion on that same launch says "Style quiz / DISCOVER YOUR STYLE" and "Your recommendations / TAKE THE QUIZ FIRST".
why_it_matters: Every guest who leaves and comes back loses the work the app asked them to do, and the app greets them as a stranger while three of its surfaces disagree about what it remembers.
already_ruled: C9 — guests browse behind a soft wall
proposal_seeds: Persist guestModeOptIn across launches and land a returning guest on the home, not the gate.

title: Guest room and saves follow the next account in
observation: The room typed and the piece saved as a guest appeared under client@patina.dev — "ACTIVE ROOM / Living Room", "1 ROOM", "1 SAVED PIECE", the badge "✦ Modern Warmth" and "1 ROOMS" — for an account with zero rooms and zero saved items server-side; "Your Spaces" flags the same room "SAVED ON THIS PHONE" while every other surface counts it as account data, and it disappeared only when the local store was cleared.
why_it_matters: On the shared phone or tablet a household actually uses, one person's browsing silently becomes another person's account history, and nothing tells either of them it moved.
already_ruled: C27 names the device-scoped local store adopted by whichever account signs in next as genuinely app-side
proposal_seeds: Scope the local store to a user id and offer an explicit "keep the room and saves you made as a guest" step at sign-in.

title: Today shows 1 of 4 pending items, not the money
observation: Home shows exactly four blocks: date, 'NEXT MOVE / Review a project decision / 2 decisions need your eye.', the editorial story, and 'ACTIVE ROOM'. My Studio hub (Profile → scroll) says '4 things need your eye': 2 overdue decisions, a $4,250.00 invoice due Sep 1, and an $18,500.00 proposal expiring Sep 8. Only the decisions surface on Today. The invoice and the proposal — the two items with real deadlines and real dollars — are invisible unless I go find Profile and scroll.
why_it_matters: My whole reason to open this app is to check on my house the way I check a package. If the one screen I land on shows a quarter of what needs my attention, I still have to go hunting for the rest every single day.
proposal_seeds: Let Next Move's priority ladder surface a proposal-expiring or invoice-due branch, not just decisions and messages.

title: Every product page fails to load, no way out
observation: Tapping any card — saved or fresh — lands on 'Couldn't load product / Let's try that again.' Retrying repeats the same failure. There is no back button, no chevron, nothing else on screen.
why_it_matters: This is the one screen where I'd actually decide whether to trust a piece enough to ask Leah about it, and it never opens. I had to force-quit the app to get back to my own home screen.
proposal_seeds: Qualify the vendors embed (vendors!products_vendor_id_fkey) in the product fetch — one-line fix, per ProductAPIClient.swift:99.

title: Buy it — the dead end, verbatim
observation: My actual dead end, verbatim, is 'Couldn't load product' / 'Let's try that again' — I never got further than the broken load screen. Companion (1 tap) → 'Your recommendations' (2) → tap any card (3) → the wall. Three taps to money, and the wall isn't a wall, it's a crash. Even reading the code for what the screen would show if it loaded, the terminus is still just 'Add to Room,' and once tapped, 'Saved ✓' — no cart, no checkout, no quote, no vendor link.
why_it_matters: If I wanted to buy a $200 side table myself, without looping Leah in, there is no verb in this app for that — buying happens by proxy, through a proposal she writes, or not at all.
proposal_seeds: Fix the load trap first; then decide deliberately whether a small self-serve purchase path belongs here at all, given C24's finding that it would credit Leah nothing today.

title: No way to message my designer, anywhere
observation: 'Conversation 0 / No project conversations yet.' is the entire messaging surface — one line of grey text, no compose, no thread list, no 'message your designer' button.
why_it_matters: I have an overdue rug decision and an unpaid invoice on a $120,000 project. If I have a question, the app has no answer but 'text her outside the app' — which is exactly the email-thread loathing this app was supposed to replace.
proposal_seeds: Wire the empty Conversation block to an actual compose action, even a simple message-to-designer form, before anything fancier.

title: Two weeks away looks exactly like two minutes away
observation: After a full force-quit and relaunch, my home screen is byte-identical to the one before I left — same Next Move, same story, same 'Living Room' card. Nothing marks the gap: no last-visit timestamp, no 'while you were away,' no unread marker anywhere on the screen.
why_it_matters: This is the whole test. Can I check on my house the way I check on a package? A package tells me it moved. This screen can't tell me anything moved, even when it did — I only find out by going and re-reading every Studio row myself.
proposal_seeds: Add one honest 'since you were last here' line, computed from a real last-seen timestamp against Studio state deltas.

title: No way to say a word to the designer
observation: The entire messaging surface is a Studio block reading "Conversation  0" / "No project conversations yet." There is no compose, no thread list, no thread to open and no "message your designer" affordance anywhere in the signed-in app.
why_it_matters: A client with an overdue decision, an unpaid invoice and an expiring proposal cannot ask a single question inside the app, so every ambiguity becomes a phone call — the cost the designer was promised this would remove.
proposal_seeds: Give every project a thread that exists from day one, with a composer on the empty state.

title: Guest's day-one work is gone on day two
observation: After a force-quit the guest lands back on "Welcome home" / "Start with a piece you love" with the quiz, the portrait and the session discarded — while the Companion on that same launch still lists "Style quiz / DISCOVER YOUR STYLE" and "Your recommendations / TAKE THE QUIZ FIRST" and Profile still shows the "Warm Modern" badge.
why_it_matters: Day-2 return is the whole game, and the app greets its most invested new user by forgetting them and saying "Welcome home".
already_ruled: C9 (guests browse; soft wall)
proposal_seeds: Persist guest opt-in across launches so the second open resumes the first.

title: Today hides the four things awaiting the client
observation: The signed-in home shows one line about work — "2 decisions need your eye." — while two levels down the Studio reads "4 things need your eye" with "Decisions / 2 project choices are ready / Overdue · Aug 22", "Invoice / $4,250.00 remaining / Due Sep 1" and "Proposal / Aspen Loft — Living Room Refresh / Review by Sep 8".
why_it_matters: The only reasons this user has to open the app tomorrow — an overdue decision, an unpaid invoice, an expiring proposal — are absent from the screen they land on.
already_ruled: C23 (Today = exactly one next move) — the conflict with C2's tier-morphing home is open
proposal_seeds: Let Today's one next move carry the whole awaiting-you count and its dates.

title: No money or decision event can send a push
observation: Notifications reads "Nothing yet" / "Updates from your designer will land here." while the Studio shows an overdue decision, a $4,250.00 invoice due Sep 1 and a proposal to review by Sep 8; `apns-send` has five callers and not one touches invoices, proposals, decisions or orders.
why_it_matters: The app has no way to reach a client between opens for the only events they actually care about, so return depends entirely on them remembering.
already_ruled: C26 corrects C14 — push send is real and provisioned; nothing money-shaped calls it
proposal_seeds: Add one `invoke_edge_function('apns-send', …)` to the proposal-sent, invoice-due and decision-asked triggers.

title: The nav row back to Saved can vanish for the exact saves the app invites
observation: The Companion's "Saved" row only appears when tableItemCount > 0, and tableItemCount counts only room-scoped SavedItems (not the TableItemModel rows the piece-detail heart or an unscoped browse-card save actually creates). Saved has no other door anywhere in the app (per code read; the Companion is the sole nav surface, T13).
why_it_matters: "Find it again tomorrow" (T4) depends on a nav row that is architecturally invisible for the two most obvious ways to save a piece — heart on the detail screen, heart on an unscoped browse card — meaning a user who saves the way the UI most directly invites them to has no path back to Saved at all.
proposal_seeds: Count all TableItemModel rows for the Companion's Saved-row gate, not only room-scoped SavedItems.

title: A 6-point-wide toggle silently corrupts room data
observation: The "ft / m" unit toggle (g-25) renders "ft" at roughly 12×13pt and "m" at roughly 6×13pt — well under the 44pt minimum. Typing 18/14 with the toggle mis-hit on "m" produces no visible state change ("ft" stays bold) but silently reinterprets the entry as metres, yielding a "Living Room" of 59'×46' = 2713 sq ft, which then persists to the room view, the home Active Room card, and Profile.
why_it_matters: T5's whole premise is the room as "the object of return" — a 6-point touch target with zero feedback on activation is the root cause of a corrupted room object that then contaminates every downstream screen for the rest of the account's life.
proposal_seeds: Make ft/m a 44pt segmented control with a visible selected state; recompute (not reinterpret) already-typed values on toggle.

title: Three disagreeing 'things needing attention' counts on one screen
observation: The Studio hub header reads "4 things need your eye" and the footer reads "4 THINGS NEED YOUR EYE", directly above a block headed "Awaiting you 3" — while Today and the Companion panel both separately say "2 project decisions waiting."
why_it_matters: If a client calls to ask how many things they owe me, I can't tell them which number on the app's own screen was the right one.
proposal_seeds: Derive every attention count on every surface from one BadgeCountService total.
Compute the attention count once and reuse the same number in the header, the footer, and the Awaiting-you block.
Compute one attention count from one source and reuse it in the header, the section label, and the footer.
Compute one attention count from one source and reuse it everywhere it's displayed.
Compute one attention count in StudioQueueBuilder and read it from the home, the Companion and the footer.
Compute one attention count in one place and render it everywhere.

title: Saved opens on boards that can never fill
observation: Saved's default tab is "Boards", reading "No boards yet" / "Save pieces from recommendations to create your first board" / "Create Board" — while the Companion simultaneously reports "1 SAVED PIECE". A created board reads "This board is empty" permanently, because `CollectionsViewModel.addToBoard(_:productId:)` has no call site anywhere in the app.
why_it_matters: The default view of the only place investment accumulates is empty by construction, so the app's memory of what I love looks like nothing.
already_ruled: C28 names boards-never-hold-a-piece as fair game | C28 | C28 (already named: boards can be created but never hold a piece)
proposal_seeds: Add "Add to board" to the card menu and wire it to the existing addToBoard call, or remove Boards until it works.
Wire the card's Save/⋯ menu to call addToBoard with the active board id, or hide board creation until it does.
Default the tab to "All items" until a board exists, and wire addToBoard to the ⋯ menu.
Default to "All items" until a board can actually receive a piece.
Either wire addToBoard to a real call site (a card's ⋯ menu "Add to board") or remove the Create Board CTA until it does something.
Either wire "Add to board" into the card menu or remove boards until they can hold a piece.

title: No search exists anywhere in the app
observation: The task "Find a sofa for our living room" has no search field to answer it with. The shortest real path is Companion orb → "Your recommendations" → chip "Seating" (client-side filter over an already-fetched ≤20-row page) → card — 4 acts, and it is a filtered browse, not a search.
why_it_matters: A shopper who already knows what they want ("a sofa") is forced through an untargeted feed instead of typing the word — the single highest-intent entry to the commerce surface is missing.
proposal_seeds: Add a single search field over the catalogue, sending the category and query server-side instead of filtering twenty cached rows.
Add a text search that queries the catalog, not just filters the current page.
Add one search field over the catalogue and pass the query and category server-side.
Add a search field to Browse pieces that queries the catalog server-side, not just the current filter chips.
Add one search field to Browse pieces that sends p_category and a text term server-side.

title: A colour decision shows no colour
observation: The decision tagged "Color" — "Rug color - Natural vs Sand", "The jute rug from Studio Piet. Natural is warmer, Sand is more neutral." — presents two text-only option cards, "Natural" (badged "Recommended") and "Sand", with no swatch, no photograph and no rug anywhere on the screen.
why_it_matters: A client cannot pick a colour from prose, so the decision the designer raised to save a call generates one instead.
proposal_seeds: Render the option image or swatch the portal already holds, at card width, above each option's label.
Require at least one image per decision option before it can render as choosable.
Require at least one reference image per decision option before a designer can publish it.
Require an image per decision option and show the price difference rather than repeating the same number.

title: No Sign Out and no Delete Account anywhere
observation: Settings lists ACCOUNT ("Account", "Sign in on the web"), PREFERENCES ("Notifications", "Haptic Feedback", "Upload scans on cellular", "Appearance System"), PRIVACY & MEMORY and SUPPORT. There is no Sign Out and no Delete Account control anywhere in Profile or Settings, in guest or signed-in state; switching accounts during the walk required wiping the simulator keychain from the host. Guest Settings is byte-identical, offering an ACCOUNT section to someone with no account.
why_it_matters: An account you can create in the app and cannot leave or delete is both a trust failure for a cautious buyer and an App Store 5.1.1(v) exposure.
proposal_seeds: Wire the Account row to AccountView, which already contains the sign-out alert.
Surface Sign Out (and Delete Account) directly in Settings rather than only inside the unreachable Account screen.
Restore the Account screen so its existing Sign Out alert is reachable, and add account deletion.
Fix the Account row's navigation and add an account-deletion request to it before any purchase ships.

title: Same story forever, permanently marked unread
observation: Every lane, every tier and every relaunch shows the same card: "4 MIN READ" with a clay dot in the corner, "MAKER SPOTLIGHT / The Grain Whisperer of Maine / Jonathan Chilton on 40 years of listening to wood".
why_it_matters: The one editorial surface that could be an honest variable reward never rotates, and its freshness marker is hard-coded true — a fabricated "new".
already_ruled: C5 honesty rule; C28 names the hard-coded isUnread as fair game | C28 | C5 (honesty: no fabricated signals), C28 (already named as an honesty candidate) | C5 (no fabricated signals); C28 names the hard-coded dot
proposal_seeds: Persist a per-story read timestamp locally and drive the dot from it.
Derive isUnread from a real last-viewed timestamp per user.
Persist a read timestamp per story id and drive the dot from it.
Derive the dot from a stored last-read story id and stop serving one row forever.

title: Notification permission asked once, unexplained
observation: Authorization is requested exactly once per install, immediately after the first successful design-request submission, with no pre-permission screen and no rationale copy; the only related control is a Settings toggle labelled "Notifications" that writes a profile preference, not the OS grant, and reads ON for a guest who can receive none.
why_it_matters: Someone who never submits a request is never asked, so the app has no way to reach the majority of its readers for the rest of the install's life.
already_ruled: C28 names the single unexplained prompt as fair game | C28 (permission asked once, only after a design request, no pre-permission copy) | C28 names the single-prompt behaviour
proposal_seeds: Ask at the first genuinely notify-worthy moment — the first save or the first room — with one line naming what will be sent.
Earn the prompt on the first real event — a decision or a shipment — with one sentence naming exactly what will be sent.
Ask at the first real event — a proposal or invoice arriving — with one plain sentence naming what will be sent.
Ask at the first money-shaped moment — "tell me when this ships" or "remind me before it's due" — with one line of rationale first.

title: Deadlines shown on list cards vanish on the detail screen the client acts on
observation: "Due Sep 1, 2026" appears on the invoices list card and is absent on the invoice detail screen itself; the same pattern reproduces for the proposal ('Expires Sep 8' on the list, dropped on detail) and the decisions ('Overdue · Aug 22' on the Studio hub, dropped on the decisions list).
why_it_matters: The screen a client actually acts on — where they decide whether to pay now or later — is the one screen that doesn't tell them the deadline, which pushes the urgency question back to me.
proposal_seeds: Carry the due/expiry line onto the detail header, beside the amount.
Put "Due Sep 1" directly under the balance on the invoice detail, and turn it red once past due.
Carry the due/expiry/overdue label from the list card through onto its own detail screen.
Render the due/expiry date in the header of every money detail screen.

title: The orb covers the button it should help with
observation: The fixed circular Companion control sits on top of the primary action on multiple screens: it clips "Sign proposal" on the proposal detail, clips "Browse Picks for This Room" on the room, and at XXL the proposal's "Space Plan" body text runs directly under it and is cut off mid-sentence.
why_it_matters: The one control the app calls navigation obscures the two acts that matter most — signing and browsing — and gets worse at larger type.
already_ruled: C23 — Option B reserves the hearth as layout space; app content is not meant to render beneath the Companion | C23 Option B contract: "The Hearth is reserved layout space… App content does not render beneath the active Companion shape." — this is that contract not being honoured | C23 (Option B: "App content does not render beneath the active Companion shape") — the contract is ruled and violated here
proposal_seeds: Reserve the 120 pt hearth as bottom padding on every scroll view that owns a primary action.
Make the 120 pt hearth a real bottom inset on every screen that draws a primary action.
Apply the 120pt hearth inset to every scroll container, not just the home.

title: 'Your studio' promises three things, delivers one
observation: The Companion's row reads 'Your studio / PROJECTS · MESSAGES · DECISIONS.' Tapping it lands directly on a bare projects list with a search bar — no messages, no decisions, no path to the real Studio hub (which lives only via Profile).
why_it_matters: The app's only nav surface just told me where I'd land and was wrong. That costs trust in every other row in that same menu.
proposal_seeds: Point the "Your studio" row at StudioHubView, or rename it to what it opens.
Either route 'Your studio' to the same StudioHubView Profile uses, or rename the Companion row to 'Projects'.
Point the Companion's 'Your studio' row at the actual Studio hub (StudioHubView), not the bare projects list.

title: A typed form calls itself a scan
observation: The Next Move promises "A short scan gives the Companion a real space to work from." and opens a typed form. The summary then offers "Rescan" and reports "0 ITEMS DETECTED" for a room nobody scanned; Your Spaces stamps the room "JUST SCANNED" directly above its own caption "2713 SQ FT · MANUAL ENTRY"; the Studio lists it as "Living Room / SCANNED AUG 26".
why_it_matters: Four surfaces claim a capture that never happened, which is the fastest way to make a buyer distrust everything else the app claims to know about his house.
already_ruled: C5 honesty; C12 as corrected — the manual route is a first-class path, not a degraded scan | C12 (manual entry is the ruled non-LiDAR fallback) — the fallback is ruled, the scan vocabulary on it is not
proposal_seeds: Give the manual route its own vocabulary end to end — entered, edit, no detected-items stat.
Give the manual path its own vocabulary — "Edit details", "Entered by you" — and drop the scan chips and detection counts.
Use language that's honest about the entry method, e.g. "Your room is saved" for the manual-entry fork.

title: Nothing on a piece helps you decide
observation: The full apparatus for deciding on a piece is the card menu — "Save", "Share", "Not for me", "View details". There is no compare surface anywhere in the app; `TableItemModel.notes` exists and no UI writes it; and the piece screen carries no "Get design help" control, though that CTA appears on eleven other surfaces.
why_it_matters: Deciding between two chairs is the actual job, and the app helps with none of it — least of all with asking a human about the thing you are looking at.
proposal_seeds: Put "Ask a designer about this piece" in the piece-detail action bar, pre-scoped to the piece.
Put "Ask your designer about this piece" on the piece screen, carrying the product id into the message.
Let Saved select two pieces and show them side by side with price, maker and materials.

title: The shared link cannot open the app
observation: The app declares only the custom scheme `patina` in Info.plist and carries no `com.apple.developer.associated-domains` entitlement, so the `https://app.patina.cloud/library/<id>` link it hands out opens Safari even for someone with Patina installed.
why_it_matters: Every off-app trigger — a share, an email, a future push landing page — dead-ends in a browser instead of returning someone to the app.
already_ruled: C28 (no associated domains named as a standing gap)
proposal_seeds: Add the associated-domains entitlement and map /piece/<id> to the existing deep-link handler.
Add associated domains for patina.cloud and route `/library/<id>` to the piece detail.
Add associated domains so every Patina link opens the app when it is installed.

title: No partner, household or second seat
observation: There is no way to share a room, a board or the Saved list — the three ShareLink sites are all single-product links. There is no invite flow, no household model, no co-viewer and no second-seat concept anywhere in the app, and no household or family-member table exists across all 487 migrations.
why_it_matters: Furniture is bought by households, not people; a product that can only hold one of a couple will be abandoned by the one it excludes.
proposal_seeds: Start with one shared list per household — an invite link that grants a second account read/save access to the same Saved rows.
Add a single "invite your partner" seat scoped to rooms, saved items and project read access.
Scope a single "invite your partner to this project" seat before any broader sharing model.

title: "Account >" has a chevron and does nothing
observation: The Settings row "Account" draws a chevron and does not navigate — tapped dead-centre of its 338×44 frame with the screen unchanged, reproduced independently in the guest tier twice and the signed-in client tier once. `AccountView` exists in the codebase.
why_it_matters: A dead control on the account screen is the one place a cautious user checks first, and it is the app's own promise that nothing here is dead.
already_ruled: C5 — no dead controls | C5 (no dead controls)
july_status: regression-class — U05 delivered "all 7 named dead controls wired or removed"; this row is inert on the walked build | U05 DELIVERED-CODE (all 7 named dead controls wired or removed) — this is a regression or a site not in that set
proposal_seeds: Fix the push to AccountView, or remove the row until it navigates.
Wire the row to AccountView, or delete the row.
Either build the Account screen or remove the row until it does.

title: "Your budget" shows one invoice, not the client's real $725,000 across projects
observation: "Your budget / ACROSS YOUR PROJECTS" shows "$4,250 BILLED / $0 PAID / $4,250 OUTSTANDING" — the total across this client's three actual projects (Birch Hollow $185,000 + Aspen Loft Refresh $120,000 + Marrow & Vale $420,000) is $725,000, and only one of the three projects appears.
why_it_matters: If a client opens the one screen labelled 'budget across your projects' expecting to see the number we agreed to, and sees a figure 1/171st the size, that's a very reasonable phone call to my studio to ask what happened to their money.
proposal_seeds: Rename the screen to what it computes — billed versus paid — and show project budget separately.
Roll up the client's true project totals before calling the screen a budget, or rename it to 'This invoice'.

title: Studio rows unreachable by VoiceOver
observation: scan_ui on the Studio block returns none of Decisions, Invoice, Proposal, Active projects, Proposals, Invoices, Budget or Archive as accessibility buttons — only "Open Living Room", "Retake Style Quiz", "Get design help", "Settings" and Back. The rows draw chevrons and respond to taps. Reproduced in dark; at Dynamic Type XXL the same rows do expose a button role.
why_it_matters: The client's entire money and decision inbox is invisible to VoiceOver and Switch Control at default text size, so an assistive-tech client cannot sign or pay at all.
proposal_seeds: Make every Studio queue row a real Button with an accessibility label and hint at all text sizes.
Add explicit accessibility labels/traits to each Studio row so they register as buttons to VoiceOver.

title: An active project with nothing pending leaves Today
observation: The Next Move card reads "Review a project decision / 2 decisions need your eye." only while a count is above zero; the ladder is strictly ordered and, once decisions and unread messages hit zero, falls all the way back to "Return to {Room}". Proposals and invoices have no Next Move branch at all.
why_it_matters: Between the moments a designer needs an answer, a live six-figure project is invisible on the client's home screen, so the app stops being where the job lives.
already_ruled: C23 — Option B's Today is exactly one next move; the ladder's ordering is not itself ruled | C23
proposal_seeds: Give an active project a standing Today presence — phase and next milestone — under the Next Move card, independent of pending counts.
When a project is live, make the quiet-state Next Move the project's own progress, not the room.

title: No way to ask a question or defer on a decision
observation: The decision screen offers exactly two identical black 'Choose this' buttons. There's no 'ask my designer,' no 'not yet,' no way to say I need more information before an $850 choice ships.
why_it_matters: My tolerance drops the instant I have to leave the app to ask what a label means. This decision has no exit but a commitment.
proposal_seeds: Add an 'Ask my designer' link on the decision detail alongside the two choice buttons.
Add a lightweight 'Ask about this' action on the decision screen that opens a message to the designer, pre-filled with the decision context.

title: The project screen shows the designer's to-do
observation: The client's project screen prints a stat labelled "CLIENT VIEW / Milestone" — the raw `client_visibility_tier` column, shown to the client it governs — and a boxed line reading "Set up phases, payments, and FF&E in the portal →", an instruction written for the designer, rendered to the homeowner, and not a button. The rest of the screen is three stats and an Invoices row, though the app successfully fetched project_phases and the client selections and rendered neither.
why_it_matters: Seeing the setting that controls how much you are allowed to see, next to your designer's homework, makes a paying client feel like a row in somebody's database.
proposal_seeds: Delete or gate the portal-setup line behind a designer role check so it never renders for a client.
Delete both from the client build and render the phases the screen already fetched.

title: One story, forever, out of three that exist
observation: "MAKER SPOTLIGHT / The Grain Whisperer of Maine / Jonathan Chilton on 40 years of listening to wood" is the same card on the guest home, the engaged home, the activeProject home, in dark mode and after a relaunch. The fetch is `order=sort_order.desc,published_at.desc&limit=1` with no per-day or per-user selection, and the catalogue holds three stories.
why_it_matters: The single piece of content a maker-story reader would return for is the one thing on the screen that provably cannot be new tomorrow.

Serve the newest unread story per user, dated, and commission enough of them to make a weekly cadence honest.

title: "UNKNOWN MAKER" on a provenance marketplace
observation: Two of the ten curated cards print the maker line as "UNKNOWN MAKER" where others read "ROOM & BOARD", "LEE INDUSTRIES", "HOLLY HUNT", "MITCHELL GOLD + BOB WILLIAMS".
why_it_matters: The maker is the reason to buy here rather than anywhere else; an unnamed one is a piece with no story and no recourse.

Exclude products with no resolvable vendor from the curated feed rather than labelling them unknown.

title: Tomorrow the saved piece says "Add to Room" again
observation: The piece-detail save state is never seeded from storage, so a piece saved yesterday shows the primary button "Add to Room" on the next visit and saving again inserts a second row.
why_it_matters: The app forgets the single act it asks the user to perform, which is the whole basis for coming back.

Seed isSaved from the local store on appear and make toggleSave idempotent on productId.

title: AR is offered by the UI but cannot ever render
observation: The room stat row's "0 IN AR" (g-28b, c-24, d-06) is not a display bug — usdz_url is NULL::text in the recommendation RPC and hard-coded nil in the direct product fetch, so product.hasARModel is false on every code path in the app; the AR button never draws on any piece, for any account.
why_it_matters: "See it in my room" (T5) has an AR door that the UI implies exists (a stat that counts it, a Companion row named "Try in your room") but that door leads nowhere for every single product in the catalog — this is a server-contract fact, not a Simulator limitation, so it is not a device-owed unknown.

Suppress every AR-shaped affordance (button, stat, Companion row) until at least one product carries a real usdz_url.

title: "Browse Picks for This Room" is not room-filtered
observation: The room's own primary button opens the same generic "Browse pieces / 10 pieces curated for your space" grid, with no room name and no room filtering, and the rationale copy has switched to naming a different taste-portrait result than the one on Profile.
why_it_matters: The one promise that makes a scanned room worth having — pieces chosen for this space — is not kept by the button that makes it.
july_status: residual — U07 delivered room-scoped routing for this CTA; a local-only room still falls back to the unscoped marketplace
proposal_seeds: Sync the room before offering the CTA, and title the scoped grid with the room's name.
When a room has no remoteId, say so in the subtitle and offer to sync it rather than falling back silently.

title: Nothing in the app answers "where is it"
observation: The Studio's sections are "Awaiting you", "In progress", "Conversation", "Money & documents", "Archive"; there is no order, no shipment, no ETA anywhere, and the client-facing order table `direct_orders` carries only `pending_payment / paid / canceled` (+ `refunded`).
why_it_matters: The post-purchase question is the most reliable daily-return habit a furnishings app can own, and it currently has no object to attach to.
already_ruled: C24 — direct orders exist on the backend with no iOS client and no designer attribution; C11 sequences them as a ratified backlog item | C11 (direct orders are a ratified backlog item); C24 (backend exists, no iOS client, no designer attribution)
proposal_seeds: When the first order exists, give it a Today module that carries its state — and decide the designer attribution before the client ships.
Surface the BOH `fulfillment_orders` states the client already owns as a tracked item in Studio.

title: Piece-detail saves are local-only and duplicate
observation: On the standard .pieceDetail(pieceId:) route no room context is passed, so both the heart and the primary "Add to Room" button run the same local toggleSave — a TableItemModel insert with no saved_items mirror and no room. isSaved is never seeded from storage, so the same piece shows "Add to Room" again the next day and a second row is inserted.
why_it_matters: A save that never reaches the server does not survive a reinstall or reach a second device, so the shopper's whole shortlist is one uninstall from gone.
proposal_seeds: Seed isSaved from local storage on load and mirror every save to saved_items, not just room-scoped ones.
Mirror every save to saved_items with a null room, and seed isSaved from storage on appear.

title: Payment failure is one red line under a live button
observation: When the checkout hand-off fails, the screen keeps "Pay $4,250.00" in full enabled styling and inserts one line of red body text below it — "Unable to start payment. Please try again." — which shoves "Pay securely by card or bank transfer" half off the bottom edge. There is no spinner, no retry affordance and no way to reach a human about a $4,250 payment that will not start. (The 503 behind it is the known local edge-runtime fault; the failure UX is the finding.)
why_it_matters: The worst moment in the money rail is handled with less care than an empty state, on the screen where the app is asking for four thousand dollars.
already_ruled: C27 (the 503 itself is a local-environment fault and is NOT claimed here)
july_status: U29/U30 DELIVERED-CODE (PatinaErrorState + one retry label) — this site renders a bespoke red line instead
proposal_seeds: Render the canonical error state with a retry and a "contact your designer" link, and disable the button while in flight.
Render the failure as a PatinaErrorState above the button with a retry and a "contact your designer" act.

title: Designer-facing FF&E instruction rendered to the client
observation: The homeowner's project screen prints a boxed line reading "Set up phases, payments, and FF&E in the portal →" and a stat labelled "CLIENT VIEW / Milestone", the raw client_visibility_tier value shown to the client it governs. The boxed line is static text, not a button.
why_it_matters: The client sees the machinery of their own designer's tooling, which reads as unfinished software on the screen that is supposed to prove the project is under control.
already_ruled: C5 (honesty; no dead controls)
proposal_seeds: Replace the portal line with a client-voiced empty state and hide the visibility-tier stat.
Replace both with client-language empty copy that names what the designer is still preparing.

title: "CLIENT VIEW / Milestone" exposes the visibility tier
observation: A stat tile on the client's project screen is labelled "CLIENT VIEW" with the value "Milestone" — the raw client_visibility_tier the designer sets in the portal, shown to the client it governs, alongside "BUDGET $120,000" and "STATUS In Progress".
why_it_matters: Telling a client how much of their own project they are permitted to see invites the question the designer least wants asked and makes the app look like it is hiding things.
proposal_seeds: Drop the CLIENT VIEW tile from the client app entirely — it is a designer-side control, not a client-facing fact.

title: Proposal selections carry no prices and no images
observation: Under "SELECTIONS": "Walnut sectional sofa", "Hand-knotted wool rug", "Walnut coffee table", "Reading lounge chair Qty 2", "Floor lamp Qty 2" — each illustrated with the Patina wordmark glyph as a placeholder and priced at nothing, against an "INVESTMENT $18,500.00" that is never broken down.
why_it_matters: A client asked to sign for $18,500 cannot see what they are buying, so the decision moves off the app and onto a phone call with the designer.
proposal_seeds: Render each selection with its image and its line price, subtotalling to the stated investment.

title: Empty bell pitches a designer to an engaged client
observation: Under "Nothing yet" / "Updates from your designer will land here." the only control is a button reading "Get design help" — shown to a client with three projects, four proposals, an open invoice and a named designer on that invoice.
why_it_matters: The acquisition funnel is running inside an active engagement, inviting the designer's own client to request a different designer.
already_ruled: C4/U08 — the wording "Get design help" is canonical; its audience is not ruled
proposal_seeds: Suppress the design-help CTA at activeProject and replace it with "Message Leah Hartwell".

title: Matched client's Studio is five zeroes
observation: The engaged account's Studio reads "Awaiting you 0 / Nothing needs a decision.", "In progress 0 / No active projects yet.", "Conversation 0 / No project conversations yet.", "Money & documents 0 / No shared records yet.", "Archive 0 / Nothing has been archived." — under a Profile reading "0 ROOMS / 0 SAVED / — MATCH" for a user with an accepted lead and an uploaded scan on the server.
why_it_matters: The pre-project window is exactly when a designer needs the client to feel something has started, and the app shows them a wall of nothing.
july_status: U22 delivered the empty-state copy; the missing fact — the accepted lead — is new
proposal_seeds: Seed an "Awaiting you" row from the promoted design request so a matched client's Studio is never all zeroes.

title: Engaged client's only act is a second request
observation: "Your design request" opens on "No scans on this phone yet" / "You can scan a room to attach — or request design help without one below." with a single button: "Request without a scan". The already-accepted lead is not shown and there is no scan affordance on the sheet the copy points at.
why_it_matters: The title promises the status of the request the client already made and offers only the filing of a duplicate, which puts a second lead in the pool against a job a designer has already claimed.
proposal_seeds: When a non-terminal lead exists, open this sheet on the request's status and stage instead of the compose step.

title: An $850 decision commits on one unconfirmed tap
observation: "Rug color - Natural vs Sand" offers two cards, each "$850" with an identical black "Choose this" button. There is no confirmation step, no way to ask a question, no defer, no "neither", and nothing states the choice is final.
why_it_matters: The shallowest act in the app spends the client's money and commits the designer's procurement, with no recovery path for a mis-tap.
proposal_seeds: Route "Choose this" through the existing e-sign confirmation the code already contains, and add an "Ask about this" action.

title: Project detail discards the data it fetched
observation: "PROJECT / Aspen Loft Refresh / Currently: Installation & Styling" renders three stats, an Invoices row and a portal link — while the network log shows the same screen successfully loading project_phases (3827 bytes), get_client_project_selections, project_payment_milestones and list_client_proposals. No timeline, no rooms, no phases, no selections, no install date, no designer.
why_it_matters: "Where is my job" is the question this screen exists to answer, and the answer was fetched and thrown away — so the client emails the designer for a status update instead.
proposal_seeds: Render the phase timeline and the client-visible selections that are already loaded on this screen.

title: No document surface for the client
observation: "Money & documents 3" contains only "Proposals / 2 shared proposals / 1 accepted", "Invoices / 1 shared invoice" and "Budget / Project totals and payment progress". There is no Documents row anywhere in the signed-in app, and project_documents filtered to client_visible returns an empty list for this account.
why_it_matters: Floor plans, spec sheets and elevations are what a designer hands over between meetings, and the section named for documents holds none.
proposal_seeds: Add a Documents row to Money & documents that opens the existing DocumentListView, empty state included.

title: Payment failure offers no retry and no human
observation: When the checkout hand-off failed, the screen printed one line of red body text — "Unable to start payment. Please try again." — inserted below a still fully enabled "Pay $4,250.00" button, shoving "Pay securely by card or bank transfer" half off the bottom edge. No spinner, no retry control, no support affordance.
why_it_matters: A client whose $4,250 payment will not start has no next step and no one to contact, and the designer finds out when the money does not arrive.
already_ruled: C27 — the underlying 503 is a local environment fault; only the failure UX is claimed here
proposal_seeds: Render the payment error as PatinaErrorState above the button with a retry and a "Contact your designer" action.

title: Signed-in Today has zero designer/studio identity
observation: The activeProject home shows only "Today", a Next Move card, an editorial story, and an "ACTIVE ROOM" card — no designer name, no studio name, no avatar, anywhere on the screen, for a client with three real projects and a named designer of record.
why_it_matters: If I send ten clients here on ten mornings, none of their home screens ever say whose work this is — the app that's supposed to represent my relationship with them never names me.
proposal_seeds: Surface the client's studio name and avatar in the greeting header once a project exists.

title: Next Move never surfaces an open proposal or due invoice
observation: Only pending decisions and unread messages ever populate the Next Move card ("Review a project decision", "Pick up the conversation"); this client's $18,500 proposal expiring in 13 days and $4,250 invoice due in 6 days have no Next Move branch at all and are invisible on Today.
why_it_matters: My client's one daily-return reason ignores the two events I most need them to act on without me calling — a proposal expiring and an invoice going overdue.
proposal_seeds: Add a Next Move branch for open proposals and payable invoices, ranked alongside decisions and messages.

title: Companion orb covers the "Sign proposal" button
observation: On the scrolled proposal detail, the Companion orb sits directly on top of the "Sign proposal" button, clipping its own visible label to "Sign proposa".
why_it_matters: The one button that actually moves my project forward is physically obscured by the app's own persistent chrome — a client who can't find it either gives up or calls me to ask if it's broken.
proposal_seeds: Reserve bottom padding on proposal detail equal to the Companion hearth so the CTA never sits under the orb.

title: Messaging is a static "Conversation 0" with no compose or thread affordance
observation: The entire messaging surface is a count and one line: "Conversation 0 / No project conversations yet." No compose button, no thread list, no "message your designer" control anywhere in the app.
why_it_matters: A client with an overdue decision and an unpaid invoice has no in-app way to ask me a quick question — every question becomes a phone call or an email outside the product I'd be paying to reduce those.
proposal_seeds: Give the Conversation block a compose entry point that opens a real thread, not just a count.

title: Pay-invoice failure UX shoves body copy off-screen with no real retry path
observation: Tapping "Pay $4,250.00" produces "Unable to start payment. Please try again." inserted below the button in red, which pushes "Pay securely by card or bank transfer" half off the bottom edge; the button keeps full enabled styling, there is no spinner, and the only recovery offered is tapping the same button again.
why_it_matters: A client whose $4,250 payment fails silently has no in-app way to reach a human about it, and the failure state itself looks half-broken, which is exactly the moment they call my studio instead of retrying.
proposal_seeds: Move the error text above the button and add a 'Contact your designer' fallback link on payment failure.

title: Project detail leaks two designer/internal-facing strings verbatim
observation: The client's project detail shows a stat labelled "CLIENT VIEW / Milestone" (the raw client_visibility_tier column name) and a boxed link reading "Set up phases, payments, and FF&E in the portal →" — an instruction written for me, rendered to my client.
why_it_matters: My client seeing internal column labels and instructions meant for me undermines the professionalism of the whole surface, and the portal-setup link is a dead end for them since they have no portal access.
proposal_seeds: Rename the stat to a client-facing label and remove or reword the portal-setup link for the client build.

title: Notifications promises "updates from your designer" and never delivers one
observation: "Notifications / Nothing yet / Updates from your designer will land here." plus a "Get design help" button, shown to a client with a $4,250 invoice due in 6 days and an $18,500 proposal expiring in 13 days — zero notifications exist for either.
why_it_matters: The one screen with the word 'designer' in its empty-state copy is where a client would naturally check for exactly the money events I need them to notice, and it is structurally incapable of ever showing them.
proposal_seeds: Write a notification_log row on proposal-sent and invoice-due so this screen has something honest to show.

title: No dimensions, lead time, shipping, or liability fields
observation: products.dimensions JSONB exists in the schema but is neither returned by get_recommendations nor decoded by the app; there is no lead_time, stock, shipping, returns, or "who is responsible" field anywhere on the product model or the detail screen.
why_it_matters: This is exactly the information a client needs before I'd let them commit to a $2,000+ piece, and it's exactly what I get asked about when something arrives wrong — the app has nowhere to put the answer even if the detail screen worked.
proposal_seeds: Return and decode dimensions at minimum; add a shipping/returns/responsibility field to the product surface before any buy path ships.

title: No "ask my designer" control on the piece itself
observation: The piece-detail action bar has back / ? / Share / heart, and a primary "Add to Room" button — no "Get design help" control. The CTA exists on 11 other surfaces in the app but not on the screen where a client is looking at one specific piece; reaching it costs 2 acts through the Companion menu instead.
why_it_matters: The moment a client is deciding on a specific piece is exactly when I want them routed to me instead of buying elsewhere — that's the whole point of the relationship — and the app puts that option two menu levels away from the one screen where the decision is actually happening.
proposal_seeds: Add "Get design help" to the piece-detail action bar, pre-scoped to the piece the same way the room CTA is scoped to a room.

title: Decision detail: two $850 options, no image, no confirm
observation: "Rug color - Natural vs Sand" presents "Natural" (badged "Recommended") and "Sand," both priced at $850, both with no product image, each with its own identical black "Choose this" button and no confirmation step before the choice is committed.
why_it_matters: A color decision with no color shown, made irreversible on one tap with no "are you sure," is the kind of thing that gets contested after the fact on a real job — I'd rather my client call me first than tap blind on an $850 line item.
proposal_seeds: Require an image per option and a one-tap confirm step before a decision is committed and irreversible.

title: Pay-failure UX has no retry, no way to reach a human
observation: Tapping "Pay $4,250.00" that fails to start renders "Unable to start payment. Please try again." as a single line of red text inserted below the button, shoving "Pay securely by card or bank transfer." half off the bottom edge. The button keeps full enabled styling; there is no spinner, no retry control, and no way to reach support from this screen.
why_it_matters: The trigger here is a known local-only edge-function fault, not an app bug — but the response to any payment failure is app-side, and a client staring at a $4,250 deposit that silently won't start, with no next step offered, calls me, not Patina support.
proposal_seeds: On checkout-session failure, show a retry button and a "contact your designer" fallback instead of static red text.

title: No fulfillment/shipping status on any line item
observation: Invoice line items ("Dining table — deposit (50%)", "Primary bedroom nightstands (pair) — deposit (50%)") carry no shipped/delivered/damaged status. invoices (00178) and direct_orders (00276) both stop at paid/void — there is no fulfillment_status column on either.
why_it_matters: This is my exact question — "does it show up on my FF&E schedule, and can my client see where a specific piece stands" — and today the answer is no on both counts; a client with a shipped-but-not-arrived table has no way to check that from inside the app, so they call me.
proposal_seeds: Add a fulfillment_status column (unfulfilled/shipped/delivered) to the payable rail and surface it per line item.

title: Today never surfaces a proposal or invoice
observation: The Next Move ladder branches only on decisions and messages (TodayExperience.swift:95-118); there is no branch for a pending proposal or an unpaid invoice. Today for this account reads "Review a project decision / 2 decisions need your eye" with no mention of the $4,250 invoice or the four proposals.
why_it_matters: The two acts I most need a client to take without my prompting — sign, pay — are invisible on the one screen they open by default; if the app can't put money in front of them, I'm still the one who has to say "go check your invoice."
proposal_seeds: Add a proposal/invoice branch to the Next Move ladder, ranked alongside decisions and messages.

title: Deadlines shown on the list, dropped on the detail
observation: "Due Sep 1, 2026" appears on the invoices list and is absent on the invoice detail; "Expires Sep 8" appears on the proposals list and is absent on the proposal detail; "Overdue · Aug 22" appears on the Studio hub and is absent on the decisions list.
why_it_matters: The screen a client acts on — pay, sign, decide — is exactly the screen that drops the date that would tell them how urgent the act is; that's backwards for anyone managing a real procurement timeline against my schedule.
proposal_seeds: Carry the due/expiry/overdue date from each list card onto its own detail screen.

title: Budget screen shows one of three projects as "the budget"
observation: "Your budget — ACROSS YOUR PROJECTS" shows $4,250 billed for the Aspen Loft Refresh project only; the client's other two projects (Marrow & Vale Residence $420,000, Birch Hollow $185,000, per the projects list) do not appear anywhere on this screen.
why_it_matters: A screen titled "across your projects" that shows one of three is worse than not having a budget screen at all — a client who trusts the label thinks $4,250 is the whole financial picture on a $725,000 relationship.
proposal_seeds: Either roll up all projects into the budget total or rename the screen to name the one project it actually covers.

title: Messaging is a dead stub — no compose, no thread
observation: "Conversation / 0 / No project conversations yet." is the entire messaging surface for a client with an overdue decision, an unpaid invoice, and an expiring proposal — no compose control, no thread list, nothing to open.
why_it_matters: Fine by me if my client keeps calling — but it means the app takes zero email volume off my plate today despite having the routes (threadList/threadDetail) built for it; I'd rather know that clearly than assume it's doing work it isn't.
proposal_seeds: Either ship a compose/thread entry point from the Studio hub or drop the messaging block until there's a real thread to show.

title: Proposal selections show logo placeholders, no per-item price
observation: The proposal's "SELECTIONS" list — "Walnut sectional sofa," "Hand-knotted wool rug," "Walnut coffee table," "Reading lounge chair Qty 2," "Floor lamp Qty 2" — illustrates every item with the Patina wordmark glyph instead of a photo, and shows no price against any line; the $18,500 total is never broken down.
why_it_matters: I sell photography and provenance at trade margin; a proposal that shows my client five unpriced logo tiles for an $18,500 scope undersells the exact thing I'm charging for, on the document meant to close the job.
proposal_seeds: Render the selection's actual product image and unit price when the proposal item is linked to a catalog product.

title: Two quizzes give my taste two different names
observation: The Companion quiz returns "Warm Modern / YOUR TASTE PORTRAIT" after the reader chose "Warm Minimal"; the second quiz that runs after room creation asks four of the same five questions with different options and returns "YOUR STYLE, FOUND / Modern Warmth"; a third account's profile badge reads "Style Explorer".
why_it_matters: Every recommendation in the app is justified by this label, so three names for one thing makes the whole match rationale unbelievable.
already_ruled: C4 — one name per concept
proposal_seeds: Delete the second quiz and route room creation into the one taste portrait.

title: Core controls are far under 44 points
observation: The room form's unit toggles measure 12×13 pt ("ft") and 6×13 pt ("m"); the Saved screen's "Boards" tab is 46×17 pt; the trapped product screen's "Let's try that again" is 125×17 pt; the room steppers are 32×32.
why_it_matters: The 6-point control is the one that silently corrupted the room's dimensions, so undersized targets here are a data-integrity problem, not only a comfort one.
already_ruled: C23 Option B contract: "a minimum 44×44 point interactive target"
proposal_seeds: Raise every one of these to a 44 pt hit area with contentShape, starting with the ft/m toggle.

title: No Browse door on the home or in the orb
observation: The guest home shows four things — greeting, Next Move, story, Companion — and does not scroll; the Companion panel offers "Add your first space", "Style quiz", "Your recommendations / TAKE THE QUIZ FIRST" and "Sign in", with no Browse row until the quiz is finished.
why_it_matters: Someone who came to look at furniture cannot reach the furniture without first completing a personality quiz.
already_ruled: C1 no tab bar; C23 — MarketplaceLinksSection is orphaned, not ruled against, and is one mount away
july_status: residual — U24 delivered MarketplaceLinksSection persisting at every tier above discovering; it is no longer mounted by anything
proposal_seeds: Give the Companion a permanent Browse row at every tier, quiz or no quiz.

title: Active Room is a stranger's room, not mine
observation: The Active Room card reads 'Living Room / 2713 sq ft · 0 pieces saved.' I never scanned or typed that room. My real project — dining room + primary bedroom, per my own invoice's note — has no room representation anywhere. Signing out and back in (c-34) drops the card entirely, back to zero rooms.
why_it_matters: The one card that's supposed to be 'my house' on the home screen isn't. If I actually had a room in progress, I'd have no way to tell whether this card is mine or leftover from someone else's phone session.
proposal_seeds: Scope local room storage to the signed-in user id, not the device, and clear it on sign-out/sign-in.

title: Browse grid cards run off both screen edges
observation: The 2-column grid renders cards of at least four different sizes, the left column pushed partly off the left edge — one card reads only 'M & BOARD' with its price clipped mid-digit.
why_it_matters: This is the app's whole shop window. If I can't read a price or a name cleanly, I stop trusting anything else on the card, including the ones I can read.
proposal_seeds: Fix the LazyVGrid item sizing constraint so both columns share one card size.

title: My real rooms live nowhere I can check on them
observation: My invoice names 'Dining room + primary bedroom' as the scope; my decisions are about a rug and dining chairs. 'Your Spaces' shows exactly one room — 'Living Room,' 2713 sq ft, 'Manual Entry' — with no connection to either of my actual project rooms.
why_it_matters: 'See it in my room' assumes my room and my project are the same house. They're not connected at all — Your Spaces is a completely separate, empty concept from the dining room and bedroom Leah is actually furnishing.
proposal_seeds: Surface the designer-defined project rooms (from proposals/invoices) inside Your Spaces, even without a client-side scan.

title: The date you need is on the screen you leave
observation: 'Due Sep 1, 2026' appears on the invoices list, gone on the invoice detail. 'Expires Sep 8' appears on the proposals list, gone on the proposal detail. 'Overdue · Aug 22' appears on the Studio hub, gone on the decisions list.
why_it_matters: I check on my house to know 'when.' The one number I'm there for disappears exactly when I open the thing to act on it.
proposal_seeds: Carry the same due/expires/overdue line onto the detail screen for invoices, proposals, and decisions.

title: 'Budget' is really one invoice's billing total
observation: 'Your budget / ACROSS YOUR PROJECTS' shows '$4,250 BILLED / $0 PAID / $4,250 OUTSTANDING' — my single open invoice — while my Projects list totals $725,000 across three projects. Only Aspen Loft Refresh appears; Birch Hollow and Marrow & Vale don't.
why_it_matters: 'Know where the money went' is my whole reason to open this. A screen labeled 'across your projects' that only counts one invoice on one of three projects tells me the wrong number with total confidence.
proposal_seeds: Either rename this screen to what it is (invoice billing) or actually aggregate all projects' budgets.

title: A failed $4,250 payment gets one crowded red line
observation: Tapping 'Pay $4,250.00' produced 'Unable to start payment. Please try again.' inserted directly below the button, shoving 'Pay securely by card or bank transfer' half off-screen. The button keeps its full enabled look; there's no spinner and no distinct retry control besides tapping Pay again.
why_it_matters: The local 503 that triggered this is an environment fault, not a product one — but the UI it produced is real: a failed four-figure payment deserves more than a crowded caption and a button that still looks fine.
proposal_seeds: Give a failed checkout hand-off its own error state: dim the Pay button, add a real retry action, keep the reassurance copy visible.

title: Nothing that matters to me can be shared
observation: The only Share buttons anywhere in the app are on catalog pieces. My rug decision, my $18,500 proposal, and my $4,250 invoice — the actual open items on my house — have no share control at all.
why_it_matters: If I want my husband's opinion on 'Natural vs Sand' before I tap 'Choose this,' there is no way to hand him the decision from inside the app — I'd screenshot it myself.
proposal_seeds: Add a Share action on decisions at minimum — the highest-stakes, most time-sensitive screen a second household member would want to weigh in on.

title: Dark mode: no Pay button in sight
observation: The dark-mode invoice detail, scrolled to the same 'No payments recorded yet' point that shows 'Pay $4,250.00' in light mode, has no visible Pay control at that stop — just the dimmed Companion orb and the footer.
why_it_matters: This is exactly when I'd be paying an invoice — after the kids are asleep, phone brightness down. If the button isn't where I expect it, I might assume the app is broken and text Leah to ask how else to pay.
proposal_seeds: Verify the Pay button's dark-mode contrast/visibility at this exact scroll depth on device.

title: XL type: the Dynamic Island blots out my proposal's title
observation: At Dynamic Type XXL, the scrolled Studio list's top card — 'Aspen Loft — Living Room Refresh / Review by Sep 8' — is fully covered by a solid black status-bar pill drawn over the content, no safe-area inset reserved.
why_it_matters: I'm 47, and larger text is a real setting for me, not an edge case. At that size the one line I need — which proposal, and by when — is the line that's covered.
proposal_seeds: Reserve a top safe-area inset on the scrolled Studio list so content never draws under the status bar/Dynamic Island.

title: Fresh install is met by a wall, not a room
observation: The first real screen after a blank splash is a full-screen gate: "Welcome home" / "Start with a piece you love", then "Sign in with Apple", "Continue with Google", "Continue with email", a divider reading "or", and only then "Look around first →", with "Have a password? Sign in" beneath it.
why_it_matters: A skeptical buyer decides in three seconds whether an app is for him or for its own funnel, and the door he wants is the fourth option under a divider.
already_ruled: C9 (auth = Supabase, passwordless-first + soft wall, guests browse) — the soft wall is ruled; the gate-first-screen ordering is shipped behaviour, not ruled copy
proposal_seeds: Promote "Look around first" above the divider as the primary act on first launch.

title: Unit toggle is a 6-point silent target
observation: The "ft / m" control in the ROOM DIMENSIONS header exposes "ft" at 12×13pt and "m" at 6×13pt. Tapping "m" produced no visible state change — "ft" stayed bold — while silently changing how the typed numbers were interpreted. Steppers are 32×32.
why_it_matters: A six-point target with no visible state is how a sixty-three-year-old's room gets recorded at four times its size without him ever seeing a control change.
already_ruled: C23 (Option B trust contract: controls at least 44×44 points)
proposal_seeds: Make ft/m a 44pt segmented control with an unmistakable selected state.

title: "0 IN AR" counts a feature that cannot exist
observation: The room stat row reads "0 ITEMS", "— MATCH", "0 IN AR", with "IN AR" undefined on screen. `usdz_url` is `NULL::text` in the recommendations RPC and hard-coded nil in the direct product fetch, so `hasARModel` is false on every code path: the AR button never draws, and the two remaining doors land on "3D model not available for this product".
why_it_matters: The app advertises a placement feature it structurally cannot deliver, on the screen that is supposed to prove it knows the room.
already_ruled: C28 (usdz_url always NULL so AR never renders)
proposal_seeds: Hide the AR stat and the AR doors until a product actually carries a model. What would settle this: a device pass with ARKit available on a product row seeded with a real usdz_url — the Simulator cannot run ARKit, so only the null-column half is proven here.

title: Design help offers a second request, not status
observation: "Your design request" opens on "No scans on this phone yet" / "You can scan a room to attach — or request design help without one below." with a single button, "Request without a scan" — for an account whose request has already been accepted. The sheet offers scanning while carrying no scan affordance.
why_it_matters: A homeowner waiting on a designer is invited to file a duplicate request instead of being told where the first one stands.
proposal_seeds: Open the sheet on the existing request's stage card when a non-terminal request exists.

title: Guest hits an escape-less wall at the last tap
observation: A guest completes the whole request — "What kind of help?", "Budget (optional)", "Timeline", "Your vision (optional)", then "Review", then "Send request" — and only then is thrown the generic gate as a sheet: "Welcome home" / "Start with a piece you love", with no Cancel, no ✕ and no "Look around first". Nothing earlier in the flow says an account will be required. Only a blind downward drag dismisses it; the draft does survive.
why_it_matters: Asking for an account at the last possible tap, in copy that never mentions the request, converts effort into resentment.
already_ruled: C9 (auth sheet presents over context and never ejects) — the ejection half holds; the missing dismiss and generic copy do not
july_status: U21 DELIVERED-VERIFIED for the Notifications entry point; this is the design-request variant, unwalked in July
proposal_seeds: Say "we'll need an account to send this" at the Review step, and give the sheet a Cancel.

title: A returning guest is forgotten and called "home"
observation: A guest's session does not survive a relaunch: the taste portrait, the quiz progress and the session are discarded with no warning, and the screen that greets them reads "Welcome home". The saved piece and the coach-mark flags do survive, so the Companion insists "Style quiz — DISCOVER YOUR STYLE" while Profile simultaneously shows the "Warm Modern" badge and "48% MATCH".
why_it_matters: Someone who spent ten minutes answering questions is erased on the second launch and greeted as a returning resident — the exact opposite of both facts.
proposal_seeds: Persist guest opt-in across launches and offer "claim your saves" at sign-in.

title: Status bar draws over scrolled content
observation: The fixed status bar draws over scrolled content with no inset reserved: "9:41" overprints "Awaiting payment" and "INV-2026-0142" on the invoice, "Invoices / 1 shared invoice" behind the Settings sheet, "Terms" on the proposal, and "Active projects" on the Studio list.
