At XXL the Dynamic Island pill itself occludes a proposal's title and its "Review by Sep 8" line, and a modal sheet's own "Close" and "Your design request" title.
why_it_matters: Dates and amounts are the words being covered, on the screens where money moves, and it gets worse at exactly the type size an older buyer uses.
already_ruled: C23 (Option B: touched screens recompose at accessibility text sizes)
proposal_seeds: Reserve the top safe-area inset on every scroll container and sheet header.

title: "Your budget" is a bill, not a budget
observation: "BUDGET / Your budget / ACROSS YOUR PROJECTS" reports "$4,250 BILLED / $0 PAID / $4,250 OUTSTANDING" and lists only Aspen Loft Refresh, for a client whose three projects total $725,000 on the projects list ($185,000 + $120,000 + $420,000). Formats mix on one card: "$4,250" above "$4,250.00".
why_it_matters: A screen headed "your budget across your projects" that omits 99.4% of the money is worse than no screen, because it will be believed.
proposal_seeds: Either rename it "Billing" or include every project's budget and committed spend.

title: An $850 choice is one tap and irreversible
observation: "DECISION / Rug color - Natural vs Sand" presents two options, "Natural" badged "Recommended" and "Sand", both "$850", both with no image — a colour decision with no colour — under two identical black "Choose this" buttons. There is no way to ask a question, to defer, or to say neither, and nothing states the choice is final. Answering is three taps from a cold home; paying an invoice is five and signing a proposal is six.
why_it_matters: The shallowest, least-confirmed act in the app is the irreversible one that spends money, and it is presented without the one thing needed to decide it.
proposal_seeds: Require the same confirm-and-sign step the app already uses, and show the option images the decision payload carries.

title: App asks who I am before showing anything
observation: First screen after the splash: "PATINA" / "Welcome home" / "Start with a piece you love" over "Sign in with Apple", "Continue with Google", "Continue with email", "or", "Look around first →", "Have a password? Sign in". No piece, no room, no story is shown before the ask.
why_it_matters: The first-open moment spends its only motivation on an account instead of on the thing that would make me want a second open.
already_ruled: C9 (passwordless-first + soft wall; guests browse)
proposal_seeds: Let the first screen be one real piece or the room prompt, with sign-in as the second beat.

title: Tour never teaches the save loop it promises
observation: The shipped tour runs two steps: "Step 1 of 2 / Welcome to Patina" — "This is your Daily Room — picks and stories chosen for your space." and "Step 2 of 2 / Your profile" — "Rooms, saved pieces, and settings live here." The declared middle step "Save what you love" / "Add pieces to a room with + Add — they follow you everywhere." never renders; its anchor `.addToRoom` mounts in no view.
why_it_matters: The one mechanic that would give a first-day user something of their own to come back to is the one the first run never explains.
already_ruled: C18 (tour copy is canonical and delivered)
july_status: residual — U32 DELIVERED-VERIFIED as copy; the middle step's anchor died with the orphaned DailyProductCard
proposal_seeds: Re-anchor step 2 on whatever control actually saves a piece today, or cut the step and say two.

title: Quiz payoff ends without a door to the pieces
observation: After five questions the result screen reads "YOUR STYLE, FOUND" / "Warm Modern" / "A STARTING POINT — REFINE IT ANY TIME.", and scrolled to the end it terminates on "Tune the portrait / Tell Patina which direction feels closer. / Tune this" — no "see your recommendations" act.
why_it_matters: The single biggest day-1 investment closes on a dead end, so the effort never converts into a habit of looking at pieces.
july_status: possible regression of U38 (quiz CTA now routes to .emergence) — what would settle this: a fresh capture of StyleResultView's full scroll with scan_ui, listing every button on the screen
proposal_seeds: Put "Browse pieces" as the result screen's primary act, above "Tune this".

title: The first ask is the app's heaviest act
observation: The only act on the first home is "NEXT MOVE / Bring your first room into Patina / A short scan gives the Companion a real space to work from." — which, without LiDAR, lands on a typed form headed "TELL US ABOUT YOUR SPACE / What kind of room?".
why_it_matters: Fogg's ability axis is lowest on day one, and the app spends that moment on a whole-room capture instead of a five-second act that could bring me back tomorrow.
already_ruled: C3 (room scan stays prominent); C23 (Today = exactly one next move)
proposal_seeds: Offer a one-tap alternative next move — save one piece — beside the room ask.

title: Home has no Browse, Saved, Studio or designer door
observation: `describe_screen` on the signed-in home returns four content elements — Next Move, editorial story, "ACTIVE ROOM", Companion bubble — and swiping up changes nothing; there is no tab bar, no nav bar, no "Browse pieces", no "Saved", no "Get design help" and no Studio row anywhere on the screen.
why_it_matters: Every place my accumulated investment lives is now reachable only through an unlabeled orb or an unlabeled monogram, which is a tax on every single return.
already_ruled: C23 (Option B accepted; the July rail is orphaned, not ruled over — C2 vs C23 is an open ruling for Kody)
july_status: regression — U24 (MarketplaceLinksSection persists at every tier), U23 ("All rooms →" chip on home) and U44 (home footer links) were DELIVERED-VERIFIED and are unmounted at 3cd84ecb3
proposal_seeds: Re-mount one persistent doors row under Today's three modules, inside the Option B contract.

title: A saved piece forgets it was saved
observation: The piece-detail primary button reads "Add to Room" and flips to "Saved ✓" only for the life of the screen: `toggleSave` inserts a local `TableItemModel` with no remote mirror, `isSaved` is never seeded from storage, and re-saving inserts a second row.
why_it_matters: An app that cannot show me what I already chose cannot use my own choices as the reason to come back.
july_status: residual — DELIVERY.md names "Add-to-Room gives no visible feedback and no confirmed saved_items row" as an open follow-up
proposal_seeds: Seed `isSaved` from storage on appear and mirror every save to `saved_items`.

title: Home says zero pieces saved while Saved holds one
observation: The home card reads "ACTIVE ROOM / Living Room / 2713 sq ft · 0 pieces saved" on the same device and session where "Saved / All items" lists "ROOM & BOARD / Heirloom Oak Dining Table / $4200".
why_it_matters: The one module on Today that could show accumulation — "your room is one piece closer" — reports zero, so investment never becomes visible progress.
proposal_seeds: Count unscoped saves toward the active room until a real room attachment exists.

title: My investment belongs to the phone, not the account
observation: "Your Spaces" tags the room "SAVED ON THIS PHONE" and "2713 SQ FT · MANUAL ENTRY" while Profile, the Companion and Today all count it as account data ("1 ROOMS", "1 SAVED PIECE"); after the local store was cleared the same account showed "0 ROOMS / 0 SAVED / — MATCH".
why_it_matters: Everything the app remembers about me can vanish with a reinstall or a new phone, which makes the accumulated-value story that drives long-run return untrue.
proposal_seeds: Mirror rooms and saves to the account on sign-in and claim the guest store explicitly.

title: Project screen shows three stats and no timeline
observation: "PROJECT / Aspen Loft Refresh / Currently: Installation & Styling" then "BUDGET $120,000", "STATUS In Progress", "CLIENT VIEW Milestone", an "Invoices / View and pay your invoices" row and a link — no phases, no dates, no rooms, no selections, though the screen successfully fetched `project_phases` and `get_client_project_selections`.
why_it_matters: "Has anything moved?" is the question that brings a mid-procurement client back, and the screen that should answer it renders none of the data it already has.
proposal_seeds: Render the fetched phases as a dated timeline with the current phase marked.

title: The whole Studio hides behind a 36pt monogram
observation: The only route to projects, proposals, invoices, budget and decisions is the unlabelled circular "C" in the top-right corner of the home, then a scroll past the avatar and stats to "STUDIO / The work around your home, in one place."
why_it_matters: Every reason an activeProject client has to open the app is three acts and one unlabelled corner glyph away, which is the opposite of a habit loop.
already_ruled: C1 (no tab bar; Companion + hub rail are the nav)
proposal_seeds: Give the Studio its own labelled door on Today whenever the awaiting-you count is non-zero.

title: Deadlines are printed once and never reminded
observation: The invoices list shows "INV-2026-0142 / $4,250.00 / Due Sep 1, 2026"; the invoice detail I act on drops the due date entirely, and the app contains no `UNNotificationRequest` of any kind, so it cannot remind me itself.
why_it_matters: A dated obligation is the most honest return trigger a client app can have, and this one exists only on a card the user has already left.
proposal_seeds: Print the due date on the detail and offer one local reminder the user opts into.

title: Returning client is offered to re-file their request
observation: The sheet titled "Your design request" reads "No scans on this phone yet" / "You can scan a room to attach — or request design help without one below." with the single act "Request without a scan" — for an account whose request was already accepted and claimed.
why_it_matters: A returning engaged client is shown the beginning of a journey they already finished, which reads as the app losing their file.
proposal_seeds: Route an existing non-terminal request to its status screen instead of the compose sheet.

title: Only one piece can be shared with anyone
observation: The card menu offers "Save", "Share", "Not for me", "View details" — and there is no share on a room, a board, or the Saved list anywhere in the app.
why_it_matters: Couples decide on rooms, not on single chairs, so the app cannot participate in the conversation that actually precedes a purchase.
proposal_seeds: Make a room shareable as a read-only page before making anything else shareable.

title: The app owns no surface outside itself
observation: The Xcode project declares three targets — app, unit tests, UI tests — and no app extension of any kind: no WidgetKit, no ActivityKit, no AppIntent, no NSUserActivity, no local notification, no background refresh.
why_it_matters: Every return has to start inside the user's own memory, because the app has no quiet place on the Home Screen, Lock Screen or in Spotlight to remind them it exists.
already_ruled: C28 (no widget/App Intent/Live Activity/associated-domains)
proposal_seeds: Ship one small Home Screen widget showing the active room and the awaiting-you count.

title: The editorial well holds three stories
observation: "MAKER SPOTLIGHT / The Grain Whisperer of Maine" is served by an unfiltered query for the single highest `sort_order` row, and the whole `editorial_stories` table holds exactly the three rows seeded by its own migration.
why_it_matters: The one module that could honestly be new every morning has no supply behind it, so an editorial answer to daily return is a content commitment, not a code change.
already_ruled: C3 (editorial feel of the Daily Room)
proposal_seeds: Decide the publishing cadence and the writer before Today leans any harder on the story.

title: Tour skips the app's only save-loop lesson
observation: Tour shows "Step 1 of 2 / Welcome to Patina" then jumps straight to "Step 2 of 2 / Your profile" (g-09, g-10). The promised middle step — "Save what you love" / "Add pieces to a room with + Add — they follow you everywhere" — never appears; the Companion intro card ("I'm your Companion.") presents immediately after (g-11).
why_it_matters: A first-time user is never taught the app's save/room-building loop before the Companion becomes the sole teacher, which then does not teach it either (its intro is a generic "I'll show you the way," not the save mechanic) — the exact mechanic T4/T5 assume the user already understands.
already_ruled: C8 correction (canon digest §6): sequencing is aspirational, not delivered; DELIVERY.md residual, unaddressed through the final hardening wave
proposal_seeds: Re-anchor tour step 2 on a control that exists on the shipped Today surface, or drop the step and its promise together.

title: Saved opens on a tab that says nothing is saved
observation: "Saved" opens on the "Boards" tab by default, reading "No boards yet" / "Save pieces from recommendations to create your first board" (g-21) — for an account that has one real saved item sitting one tap away under "All items" (g-22b).
why_it_matters: T4's whole premise is "find it again tomorrow" — the surface built for exactly that opens on an empty-looking screen even when the thing you're looking for is there, one tab over.
proposal_seeds: Default Saved to whichever tab is non-empty, or to "All items" until a board actually holds something.

title: The only door to the Studio is the worst-reached control on the screen
observation: The three top-right glyphs (bell, ?, monogram) sit as ~36pt targets in the far top-right corner (g-12, x-01) — the single hardest zone to reach one-handed on a phone this size — and the monogram is the sole door to Profile → Studio, the surface holding every project/proposal/invoice/decision the app knows about.
why_it_matters: The Companion orb (the app's best-placed control, per its own 120pt bottom hearth) can reach almost everything else in the app in one tap; the one thing it structurally cannot reach for an activeProject client without a detour is the Studio, which sits behind the one control placed for the least reachable hand position.
proposal_seeds: Add a Studio door to the Companion panel's universal tail, or move the monogram into the bottom hearth's reach zone.

title: The status bar draws over scrolled content, worst on modal sheets at XXL
observation: In dark mode, the fixed status bar (9:41, signal icons) draws over the scrolled Studio list — the clock sits directly on "Review by Sep 8" (d-02). At XXL Dynamic Type the Dynamic-Island pill itself, not just the clock digits, occludes the top proposal's title (x-02). A third reproduction lands on a modal sheet: the "Your design request" sheet's own "Close" button and title overlap the 9:41 clock at XXL (x-06).
why_it_matters: This is a systemic missing safe-area inset, not one screen's bug — it reproduces on a plain list, on the same list at a different type size, and on a completely different component (a sheet), which means any new scrollable surface is likely to inherit it.
proposal_seeds: Audit every scrolled list and sheet header for a top safe-area inset; this looks like one shared layout omission, not several.

title: The filter chip row overflows the screen at XXL with no way to reach the last chip
observation: At Dynamic Type XXL, the chip row (All / Seating / Tables / Lighting / Storage) runs off the right edge — "Storage" is clipped to "Stor" with no visible scroll indicator or affordance suggesting more chips exist (x-03).
why_it_matters: A user on the accessibility text size this row was supposedly built to survive (per the code's own accessibility-size branches elsewhere) cannot select the Storage filter at all — the control is present but physically unreachable.
proposal_seeds: Wrap the chip row or make it a horizontally scrolling ScrollView with a fade/arrow hint at XXL.

title: Body text runs into the Companion button with no reserved space
observation: At XXL, the "Space Plan" section's wrapped body text ("Conversation seating around the fireplace,...") is cut off directly by the fixed circular Companion button at the screen's bottom edge, with no bottom padding reserved for it (x-05).
why_it_matters: The Companion hearth is described elsewhere as "reserved layout space, not a persistent visible bar" — here it behaves like neither: it isn't reserved (content runs under it) and it isn't avoided (it clips the last visible line), the worst of both.
proposal_seeds: Give scrollable content a bottom inset equal to the Companion hearth's height at every Dynamic Type size.

title: Home doesn't scroll, and gives no sign anything is hidden
observation: For the activeProject account (3 projects, 4 proposals, 1 open invoice, 2 pending decisions), d-01 (top) and d-02 (after a swipe) are pixel-identical — the screen has no more content to reveal, so the swipe simply does nothing.
why_it_matters: A screen with real, current, dollar-figure work waiting (T13's "one-handed on the bus" reader would want exactly this) offers no scroll cue, no "more below" affordance, and no indication that four pending items exist two acts away behind the monogram — it just ends.
proposal_seeds: If Today truly has nothing more to show, say so; if the Studio surface should be reachable from here, mount it.

title: There is no Sign Out control anywhere in the app
observation: Neither Settings nor Profile carries a Sign Out action for a signed-in client. The only way to end a session is to force-quit and wipe the device keychain from outside the app — not performable by an end user.
why_it_matters: Switching or removing an account is table-stakes account-management, and its total absence blocks the household scenario T12 depends on (a second person on the same phone) as much as it blocks simple account hygiene.
proposal_seeds: Add Sign Out to Settings (the working AccountView code already has the alert copy written — it just has no live door to it, per the Account-row finding above).

title: Two different quizzes exist for one concept and disagree with each other
observation: The Companion-entry quiz's first question ("Which palette feels like home?", g-06) offers Warm Minimal / Cool Modern / Classic Comfort / Eclectic Curated. The quiz reached after manually entering a room ("Which room speaks to you?", g-26) offers Warm Minimal / Cool Modern / Layered Comfort / Curated Mix — two of four options differ, for what the app treats as the same StylePreferenceModel.
why_it_matters: A user who takes both (easy to do, since the room-creation flow surfaces its own quiz unprompted) gets two different taste labels for one underlying preference, with no indication either quiz knows the other exists.
proposal_seeds: Collapse to one quiz asset reused by both entry points, or make the second entry point resume the first quiz's answers instead of re-asking.

title: The design-request soft wall removes every escape hatch the real gate has
surface: AuthScreenView presented as a mid-flow sheet
observation: The generic auth gate (g-02, s-01) offers Sign in with Apple, Continue with Google, Continue with email, and "Look around first." The same screen thrown mid-flow as a soft wall after "Send request" (g-35) is missing "Look around first" and has no Cancel or X anywhere — only a blind downward drag dismisses it, and nothing on the sheet mentions the request that triggered it.
why_it_matters: A first-time guest who just finished a multi-step design request hits a wall with strictly fewer exits than the app's own front door, at the exact moment they're most likely to feel trapped rather than invited to sign in.
proposal_seeds: Give the soft-wall variant of AuthSheet an explicit Cancel/X, and name the thing it's gating ("Sign in to send your request").

title: Dimensions exist as a column and nowhere else
observation: products.dimensions jsonb {width,height,depth,unit} exists in the schema; get_recommendations does not return it, ProductModel does not decode it, and no product surface prints a measurement. A live count over the local catalog returns dimensions on 0 of 21 rows.
why_it_matters: Nobody buys a sectional they cannot measure against a wall, so the absence of dimensions blocks the highest-value purchases outright.
proposal_seeds: Return dimensions from get_recommendations, decode it, and print one W x D x H line under the price.

title: Lead time never reaches the shopper
observation: products.lead_time_weeks exists but is CHECK-required only for layer='studio'; the catalog layer the client app reads has no lead-time guarantee. The RPC does not return it, the app does not decode it, and locally it is populated on 1 of 21 rows.
why_it_matters: "When would it arrive" is the question that decides a furniture purchase, and the app cannot answer it for any piece.
proposal_seeds: Require lead_time_weeks on catalog-layer rows and print it as a range beside the price.

title: No shipping, returns or responsibility copy exists
observation: No column on products carries shipping, delivery, returns or liability, and no screen in the app prints any of it. The closest thing to a policy anywhere in the client is the proposal's terms: "Deposits are non-refundable once procurement begins. Custom items are final sale."
why_it_matters: A homeowner asked to spend thousands cannot see who is responsible when a piece arrives damaged, which is the exact risk that keeps people on a retailer they already trust.
proposal_seeds: Add one shipping-and-returns block to the piece detail, sourced from a per-vendor policy row.

title: The maker line shows the retailer, not the maker
observation: The card for "Heirloom Oak Dining Table" is labelled "ROOM & BOARD"; the same row's products.brand column reads "Nordic Atelier" and is never returned or shown. Fourteen of twenty-one local products have no vendor_id at all and render "UNKNOWN MAKER".
why_it_matters: On a marketplace whose whole pitch is provenance, the byline names a national retailer or nobody, which is the opposite of the trust the brand is selling.
proposal_seeds: Source maker_name from products.brand with the vendor as fallback, and never print "Unknown Maker" on a published piece.

title: Provenance layer renders empty on every product
observation: The detail's maker-location tag and "maker story" card read from vendors.made_in and vendors.brand_story. A live count over the local stack returns 0 of 104 vendors carrying made_in and 0 of 104 carrying brand_story, so both surfaces have nothing to render for any of the 21 products.
why_it_matters: Provenance is the reason to buy here instead of the maker's own site, and there is no provenance content behind the component that is supposed to carry it.
proposal_seeds: Make made_in and brand_story required before a vendor's products can be published to the catalog layer. What would settle this: the same two counts against Strata, which this program could not read.

title: Saving a piece gives no visible confirmation
observation: After tapping a card's heart the icon stays outlined and unfilled, with no toast, no count change and no "saved to" line; the dark lane tapped hearts twice and Saved stayed empty.
why_it_matters: The one investment the app asks for on the commerce path gives no receipt, so the shopper cannot trust that tomorrow's list will hold anything.
july_status: residual — DELIVERY.md names "Add-to-Room (+ Add) gives no visible feedback and no confirmed saved_items row" as an open follow-up
proposal_seeds: Fill the heart optimistically and show one line of confirmation naming where it was saved.

title: Saved opens on an empty tab while an item exists
observation: Saved opens on "Boards", which reads "No boards yet / Save pieces from recommendations to create your first board" and a "Create Board" button, while the Companion row that led here said "Saved / 1 SAVED PIECE" and the item sits one tab over under "All items".
why_it_matters: The screen a returning shopper opens to find yesterday's piece tells them they have saved nothing.
proposal_seeds: Default to "All items" whenever there are saved pieces and no boards.

title: The Saved door vanishes for pieces saved from Browse
observation: The Companion's "Saved" row is returned only when context.tableItemCount > 0, and that count is computed as the sum of room SavedItems, not TableItemModel rows — so a piece saved from Browse or from the piece detail does not increment it, and the row never appears.
why_it_matters: Saved has no other door anywhere in the app, so the exact shopper the app invited to save can lose the ability to reach their saves at all.
proposal_seeds: Count TableItemModel rows in tableItemCount and keep the Saved row standing once anything is saved.

title: No "ask my designer" on the piece surface
observation: The piece-detail screen carries only back, "?", Share and heart; the ratified CTA "Get design help" appears on eleven other surfaces and not on this one. Reaching a human about the piece being looked at costs two acts through the Companion, and only if the orb is known to be a menu.
why_it_matters: The moment a shopper hesitates over a piece is the moment the designer relationship is worth most, and the app routes them away from it.
already_ruled: C4
proposal_seeds: Put "Get design help" in the piece-detail action bar, carrying the product id into the request.

title: Buy-now is armed on the backend and unbuilt on iOS
observation: create_direct_order, create-checkout-session's direct_order_id branch, the stripe-webhook settle branch and the receipt and failure emails are all live; a live count over the local catalog shows 19 of 21 products are patina_managed and therefore already pass the RPC's buyability gate. Grep finds zero iOS references to direct_order, create_direct_order or "buy now".
why_it_matters: The single highest-value gap in the product is a screen and a button, not a platform build, and every day it stays unbuilt the marketplace earns nothing.
proposal_seeds: Ship an order sheet on the piece detail that calls create_direct_order then reuses the invoice Safari-plus-poll pattern.

title: A direct order credits the designer nothing
observation: direct_orders carries no designer_id, no project_id, no commission_rate and no FF&E link; 00301_marketplace_vitals.sql:37-40 states it outright — "No designer attribution (client_id is the buyer)" — and the only designer_earnings credit path reads invoice_payments, never direct_orders.
why_it_matters: If a client buys a $3,200 sideboard in the app while a designer is engaged, the designer is paid nothing and never sees it, which is precisely the reason a designer would stop sending clients here.
proposal_seeds: Add designer_id, project_id and a snapshotted commission_rate to direct_orders in the same migration that ships buy-now, before any order rows exist.

title: No vendor link or price inquiry to leave toward
observation: products.source_url exists and is populated on 9 of 21 local rows; it is never returned by the RPC, never decoded and never shown. There is no "where to buy", no "ask about this piece" and no maker page anywhere in the app.
why_it_matters: A shopper who cannot buy in the app and cannot see who sells the piece leaves to a search engine, and the app loses the attribution and the relationship at once.
proposal_seeds: Until buy-now ships, give every piece one honest outbound act — "Ask about this piece" — that files a scoped request.

title: The order state machine stops at "paid"
observation: direct_orders.status is CHECK-constrained to pending_payment, paid and canceled (plus refunded from 00277). There is no fulfillment status, no shipped_at, no delivered_at, no tracking number and no ETA column.
why_it_matters: Without shipping states there is nothing to notify about and nothing to come back for after the money moves.
proposal_seeds: One migration adding fulfillment_status with the fulfillment-notify vocabulary plus shipped_at, delivered_at and tracking_number.

title: Two budgets for one project, both labelled budget
observation: "BUDGET $120,000" appears on the Aspen Loft project detail while "BUDGET / Your budget — ACROSS YOUR PROJECTS" reports "$4,250 BILLED / $0 PAID / $4,250 OUTSTANDING" for a client whose three projects total $725,000. Formats mix on one card: "$4,250" above "$4,250.00".
why_it_matters: When the app gives two different answers to "what does this cost me", every other number it shows becomes negotiable.
proposal_seeds: Rename the billing summary "Billed to date" and give budget its own project-scoped figure.

title: Due date dropped from the pay screen
observation: "Due Sep 1, 2026" is printed on the invoices list and does not appear on the invoice detail; the detail uses due_date only to compute the word "Past due". The same omission repeats on proposals ("Expires Sep 8" on the list, absent on the detail) and decisions ("Overdue · Aug 22" on the Studio hub, absent on the decisions list).
why_it_matters: The deadline is the reason to act now, and it is dropped from every screen where the action actually happens.
proposal_seeds: Print the due date under the invoice header and above the Pay button.

title: Card payers are told a bank transfer has started
observation: When the 60-second post-Checkout poll expires, confirmState is set to .achPending unconditionally and the banner reads "Your bank transfer has been started. Bank transfers take 3–5 business days to clear — we'll email your receipt as soon as it lands." — regardless of which rail the payer used, and regardless of whether they paid at all.
why_it_matters: A client who paid by card, or who abandoned Checkout without paying, is told a bank transfer is in flight, which is a false statement about their money.
proposal_seeds: Branch the timeout copy on the settled payment method, and default to "We haven't seen this payment yet" when none is recorded.

title: An unexplained percentage is the only progress signal
observation: Profile's stat row reads "1 ROOMS / 1 SAVED / 63% MATCH" where the same device showed "48% MATCH" before sign-in, with nothing on screen saying what is matched or why it moved; the taste portrait carries an unlabelled progress bar at roughly 45% under "WHY PATINA SEES THIS".
why_it_matters: The app's only sense of "I am getting somewhere" is a number nobody can explain, which is a progress illusion rather than earned momentum.
already_ruled: U02 established that match scores are real, not fabricated — this is about legibility, not honesty | U02/U43 — the fabricated-number half is closed; this is the unexplained-label half | C5 (no fabricated stats); U43 replaced the old "47% Style Confidence"
july_status: residual — U43 replaced the fabricated "47% Style Confidence"; the Profile MATCH stat and the unlabelled portrait bar were not part of that fix | U02 DELIVERED-VERIFIED (real varying scores), U43 DELIVERED-VERIFIED (qualitative copy) — residual is the bare percentage on the card | residual — same class as U43, on a different stat
proposal_seeds: Label the stat in words — "how close today's edit is to your portrait" — or drop it.
Replace the bare percentage with the rationale line the app already computes, or make the pill tappable to explain itself.
Say what the percentage matches, or replace it with a count of real things.

title: Filter row clips "Storage" to "Stor" at XXL
observation: At Dynamic Type extra-extra-large the chip row "All / Seating / Tables / Lighting / Storage" overflows the screen width and "Storage" is clipped to "Stor" at the right edge, with no horizontal scroll affordance visible.
why_it_matters: A category silently disappears at the text size an older buyer actually reads at.
proposal_seeds: Put the chip row in a horizontal ScrollView with a visible trailing fade.
Put the chip row in a horizontal ScrollView with a fade edge.
Put the chip row in a horizontal ScrollView with a leading fade.

title: 'Get design help' offered to a client with a designer
observation: The empty Notifications screen reads 'Updates from your designer will land here' directly above a 'Get design help' button — I already have Leah, and four things are waiting on me elsewhere in the app that this screen doesn't mention.
why_it_matters: This CTA is written for someone who's never engaged a designer. Seeing it as an existing activeProject client is a small but real 'this app doesn't know who I am' moment.
already_ruled: C17 (tier-narration empty copy is ratified) — the copy is ruled; showing the acquisition CTA at activeProject is the finding | C17 (tier-narration copy is canonical) — the copy is ruled, the tier selection is not
july_status: U22 DELIVERED-CODE (empty states name trigger + conditional CTA) — the conditional is not conditioned on tier here
proposal_seeds: Swap the empty-state CTA by tier — 'Message your designer' for activeProject/engaged, 'Get design help' only at discovering.
Swap the CTA at activeProject to "Message Leah" or the oldest waiting item.
Swap the CTA for "Message Leah" once a designer relationship exists.

title: A finished project sorts above active ones
observation: 'Birch Hollow / Completed / $185,000' sits above 'Aspen Loft Refresh / In Progress' and 'Marrow & Vale Residence / In Progress' in the Projects list. 'PHASE / Install' also truncates 'Installation & Styling' to a bare word.
why_it_matters: The project I'm mid-procurement on — the one I actually check daily — is buried under a job that's already done.
proposal_seeds: Sort active before completed, then by most recent activity.
Sort active/in-progress projects above completed ones by default.

title: No way to compare two pieces side by side
observation: There's no compare surface anywhere — code-read confirmed (grep) and consistent with what the piece-detail screen shows when it loads at all: Share, Save, a maker-story card, no comparison of any kind.
why_it_matters: 'Is this the one' is a comparison question by nature. Without it, I'm holding two tabs in my head, or texting screenshots to myself.
proposal_seeds: Add a lightweight compare (2-3 saved pieces side by side) reachable from Saved.
Let a save action target 'compare' as a lightweight two-up view, reusing the existing Saved data.

title: Coach marks cover the card they describe
observation: "Step 1 of 2 / Welcome to Patina / This is your Daily Room — picks and stories chosen for your space." fully covers the Next Move card it is describing; step 2 does the same while pointing at the profile monogram; the Companion's own "Got it" bubble then covers the panel's first row. Skip/Next render in iOS system blue, the only blue in the app.
why_it_matters: Three teaching moments in a row hide the thing being taught, on the reader's first thirty seconds.
already_ruled: C18 — tour copy is canonical; this is placement and tint, not copy | C18
july_status: residual — DELIVERY.md names the Companion-intro/tour collision as still open
proposal_seeds: Offset the bubble below its anchor and tint its controls with the app's clay, not system blue.
Offset each bubble below its anchor and tint the tour controls with the app's clay, not system blue.

title: Overdue flag dropped on the decisions list
observation: The Studio row reads "Decisions / 2 project choices are ready / Overdue · Aug 22". The decisions list it opens — "DECISIONS / Awaiting your call" — shows two cards with no date, no "asked N days ago" and no overdue marker at all.
why_it_matters: The urgency is shown on the screen the client passes through and hidden on the screen where they act.
proposal_seeds: Carry the due/overdue label onto each decision card in the list and onto the detail.

title: Onboarding never frames the app as where a client works with their designer
observation: "Welcome home / Start with a piece you love," three onboarding pages ("Every room tells a story", "See it in your space", "Find your style first"), a five-question style quiz, a two-step tour, and a Companion intro — roughly 14 taps — none of which mention a designer, a project, or an existing relationship. The one fast lane for an existing account is a small "Have a password? Sign in" link under four stacked buttons.
why_it_matters: A client I send this link to post-signature has no signal in the entire first-five-minutes flow that this is the tool for our relationship, not a furniture marketplace they wandered into.
proposal_seeds: Add one onboarding beat (or a branch off 'Have a password?') that names the app as where you work with a Patina designer you've already engaged.

title: The cheapest, most binding client act (a decision) has no confirmation step
observation: Answering a decision is 3 taps with no confirmation and is immediately final; signing a proposal is 6 taps behind a full e-sign sheet, and paying an invoice is 5 taps behind a Stripe handoff — the smallest, most casual-feeling act is the one with zero safety net.
why_it_matters: A client who fat-fingers 'Choose this' on an $850 decision has no undo, while the two acts I'd actually want deliberate friction on are already the ones that get it.

refs: artifacts/ios-daily-return-2026-08-26/research/03-walk-observations.md E2 'Money acts and their tap cost'

proposal_seeds: Add a one-tap-undo window on decisions so the friction ladder matches the money at stake.

title: The one push permission prompt fires silently, unexplained, unrelated to money
observation: Authorization is requested exactly once per install, automatically after the first successful design-request submission, with no pre-permission screen and no in-app rationale copy anywhere; a client who never submits a request is never asked at all.
why_it_matters: The one chance to earn a client's push permission is spent on a moment that has nothing to do with the proposals and invoices I actually need them to be pushed about, and it's never explained, so 'Allow' or 'Don't Allow' is a coin flip for them.
proposal_seeds: Add a one-screen rationale before the system prompt tied to a concrete promise, e.g. 'know the moment your designer sends a proposal.'

title: No way to share a room/board/status; no household or second-person concept
observation: Grep finds exactly three ShareLink sites, all sharing the same single-product URL; there is no way to share a room, a board, the Saved list, or a project/proposal/decision status, and no invite, household, partner, or co-viewer concept anywhere in the schema or client (grepped: zero household/family_member tables across all migrations).
why_it_matters: A couple deciding on a room together has no way to look at the same board or the same decision inside the app — the only thing a second person can ever receive is one product link, which stops the relationship from including them at all.
proposal_seeds: Add a read-only project/room share link so a second household member can see status without needing their own account.

title: Shared links can't open the app even when installed (no associated domains)
observation: The app declares no com.apple.developer.associated-domains entitlement and Info.plist registers only the custom scheme patina:// — so the https://app.patina.cloud/library/<id> link every share produces always opens Safari, never the app, even on a device with Patina already installed.
why_it_matters: A partner who taps the link my client shared never lands inside Patina, so any hope of a second person becoming a returning user through a share dies at the first tap.
proposal_seeds: Add the associated-domains entitlement for app.patina.cloud so shared links open the app when it's installed.

title: Notes field exists in data, never exposed in UI
observation: TableItemModel.notes and CreateSavedItemPayload.notes both exist in the data model; no view anywhere writes to either field.
why_it_matters: A client jotting "ask about this in oak instead" against a saved piece is exactly the kind of self-serve prep that would make my client meetings faster; the field is built and dead.
proposal_seeds: Add a notes field to the saved-item card and detail; the model already supports it end to end.

title: Raw internal column "CLIENT VIEW / Milestone" shown to client
observation: A stat labeled "CLIENT VIEW / Milestone" on the project detail exposes the raw client_visibility_tier column value as if it were content, on the same screen the column is meant to govern.
why_it_matters: This is internal plumbing rendered as a fact to the person it's supposed to be invisible to — it reads like a label mistake, and it's the kind of thing a sharp client (Tom's version of a client) would screenshot and ask about.
proposal_seeds: Remove the CLIENT VIEW stat from the client-facing project detail or replace it with a plain-language phase label.

title: Companion bubble clips the "Sign proposal" button
observation: On the proposal detail, the Companion bubble ("4 THINGS NEED YOUR EYE") sits directly on top of the "Sign proposal" button, visually clipping its label.
why_it_matters: This is the exact control that starts procurement on a job; the app's own persistent chrome sitting on top of it is a friction point on the single most important tap a client takes in the whole app.
proposal_seeds: Reserve bottom safe-area padding on ProposalDetailView so the Companion hearth never overlaps the primary CTA.

title: sign_proposal sends no confirmation email
observation: sign_proposal (00400_proposal_signature_authority.sql) resolves the signature and kicks off the project server-side, but the client's own API layer carries a carry-forward code comment stating the RPC does not send a confirmation email on sign.
why_it_matters: If true, neither I nor my client gets a written record the instant a six-figure scope is signed — the only way I'd know is checking The Document myself, which defeats the point of a client-facing sign flow.
proposal_seeds: Add a signature-confirmation email/notification on sign_proposal's success path, to both client and designer. What would settle this: trigger a live sign against the local stack and check the Resend/notification_log rows for a send.

title: Saved opens on an empty "Boards" tab
observation: Tapping the Companion row labelled "Saved / 1 SAVED PIECE" lands on the "Boards" tab reading "No boards yet" / "Save pieces from recommendations to create your first board"; the piece is one tab away under "All items".
why_it_matters: The screen that is supposed to prove the app remembered the investment opens by saying it has nothing.
proposal_seeds: Default to "All items" whenever the board count is zero.

title: Request sheet offers a scan it cannot take
observation: "Your design request" opens on "No scans on this phone yet" / "You can scan a room to attach — or request design help without one below." with exactly one control on the screen: "Request without a scan".
why_it_matters: The copy names the better option and provides no way to take it, so the reader submits a weaker request than the app just told them to make.
proposal_seeds: Put a "Scan a room now" secondary control on the empty state, routing to the scan flow and back.

title: Headings scroll under the status-bar clock
observation: "WEDNESDAY · AUG 26" collides with the 9:41 clock on the scrolled home, "Guest" is sliced by the screen top on Profile, and at extra-large text the Dynamic Island pill itself occludes the proposal title "Aspen Loft — Living Room Refresh / Review by Sep 8".
why_it_matters: Every scrolling surface in the app loses its own heading to the system chrome, which reads as unfinished on a product asking for four-figure trust.
proposal_seeds: Reserve the top safe-area inset on every scroll container instead of drawing content into it.

title: Room summary renders light inside dark mode
observation: With the system in dark appearance, the "YOUR SPACE / Here's what I see." summary renders on a cream ground with near-black text — the only screen in the walk to ignore the override — and its own headline washes out to near-invisible.
why_it_matters: The screen where the reader confirms the facts about their home is the one screen they may not be able to read at night.
already_ruled: C7 — dynamic dark mode via PatinaColors; camera/AR chrome is the deliberate exception and this is not that
proposal_seeds: Replace this screen's hard-coded colours with the dynamic tokens.

title: The tour's save-loop step never renders
observation: The shipped tour runs "Step 1 of 2 / Welcome to Patina" then "Step 2 of 2 / Your profile"; the declared middle step — "Save what you love" / "Add pieces to a room with + Add — they follow you everywhere." — is dropped because its anchor mounts in no view, and the "+ Add" control it names does not exist on the shipped home.
why_it_matters: The one first-run explanation of the app's save-and-return loop is silently omitted from every install.
already_ruled: C18 — the ratified 3-step tour copy is canonical; this is the delivery of step 2, not its wording
july_status: regression-class — U32 delivered the rewritten tour VERIFIED; the middle step's anchor was lost with the Option B home rewrite
proposal_seeds: Anchor step 2 to whatever control now performs the save, or rewrite it to the act that exists.

title: Dimensions and lead time never shown
observation: products.dimensions exists in the schema but is never returned by the recommendations RPC or decoded by the app; there is no lead-time or availability field anywhere the catalog reads.
why_it_matters: 'Will it fit' and 'how long will I wait' are the two things I'd actually ask before I let Leah spend $2,650 on a dining table. Neither can be answered from inside the app even when the page loads.
proposal_seeds: Add dimensions to the get_recommendations RPC output and decode it in ProductModel.

title: Saved opens on the empty tab
observation: 'Saved' opens on 'Boards,' which reads 'No boards yet' — the piece I actually saved lives one tap over, under 'All items,' a tab that doesn't default open.
why_it_matters: My first look at 'find it again' tells me nothing is there when something is. That's a wasted trip and a reason to stop trusting the count next to the Companion's Saved row.
proposal_seeds: Default Saved to whichever tab actually has content.

title: Saved can disappear from my only nav menu
observation: The Companion panel's 'Saved' row is present when I have 1 saved piece ('1 SAVED PIECE'), but the code gates it on a local room-items count, not the same count the row displays — a piece saved from Browse or the piece detail can leave the row absent entirely.
why_it_matters: The Companion is the only navigation this app has. A door that can silently stop existing means 'find it again tomorrow' sometimes has no path at all.
proposal_seeds: Gate the Companion's Saved row on the same source of truth the row's own count reads.

title: AR can never work — usdz_url is always null
observation: The room's 'IN AR' stat reads 0 in every shot I have; the RPC that feeds the catalog hard-codes usdz_url to NULL, so hasARModel is false on every code path — the AR button never draws and the Companion's 'Try in your room' says '3D model not available.'
why_it_matters: Seeing a $2,650 dining table in my actual dining room before I approve it is exactly the kind of thing that would make me trust the app with real money — it doesn't exist today, code-read, not device-tested by me. What would settle this: a device pass on a product row with a populated usdz_url.
proposal_seeds: Populate usdz_url for at least a pilot subset of the catalog before promising AR anywhere in copy.

title: The link I'd share opens the wrong app under the wrong name
observation: The one thing I can share — a piece — hands whoever I send it to a link titled 'Patina Designer Portal — app.patina.cloud.' The app has no associated-domains entitlement, so even if my husband has this app installed, that link opens Safari, not his copy of Patina.
why_it_matters: I'd be handing my own husband a link that says 'designer portal,' from an app I use as a homeowner, that can't even open his phone's copy of the app.
proposal_seeds: Give the client-facing share URL its own client-portal route and title, and add associated domains so the link opens the app.

title: Three icon systems in three stacked buttons
observation: "Sign in with Apple" carries Apple's real logo; "Continue with Google" carries a bare typed letter "G"; "Continue with email" carries a stock colour emoji envelope — three different icon systems in three adjacent buttons.
why_it_matters: The first screen of a company selling craft argues, visually, that nobody proofread it — which is exactly the doubt a $4,000 purchase cannot survive.
proposal_seeds: Replace the emoji and the typed G with monochrome SF Symbols matching the app's own weight.

title: Tour's middle step never renders
observation: The tour presents "Step 1 of 2 / Welcome to Patina" and "Step 2 of 2 / Your profile". The declared middle step — "Save what you love" / "Add pieces to a room with + Add — they follow you everywhere." — never appears, because its anchor `.addToRoom` mounts in no view and the model drops it after a 1.5s grace.
why_it_matters: The one first-run sentence that explains the app's save-and-return loop is silently omitted, and it names a "+ Add" control that does not exist on the shipped home.
already_ruled: C18 (tour content is canonical and delivered) — the copy is ruled; the dropped anchor is a named residual, not a re-proposal
july_status: U32 DELIVERED-VERIFIED — residual: the anchor was on the now-orphaned DailyProductCard
proposal_seeds: Anchor step 2 to the Active Room card and rewrite it for the save path that actually ships.

title: Says "Today" but never reads the hour
observation: The header reads "WEDNESDAY · AUG 26" over the literal word "Today". `TimeOfDay` exists with dawn/morning/day/afternoon/evening/night boundaries but is read only by the camera primer and two Companion greeting generators — never by the home.
why_it_matters: A 7:40am screen and a 9:10pm screen are identical, so the app can never feel like it was made for the moment it is being opened in.
proposal_seeds: Read TimeOfDay in the greeting header and let morning, evening and night pick different one-line copy.

title: Room summary ignores dark mode
observation: The "YOUR SPACE / Here's what I see." summary step, with "Rescan" and "This Looks Right", renders on a cream background with near-black text while the rest of the app is in dark mode — the only screen observed to ignore the system/app appearance override.
why_it_matters: A full-brightness cream screen in the middle of a dark session is physically unpleasant, and it signals that the screen was built outside the design system.
already_ruled: C7 (dynamic dark mode via PatinaDesignKit tokens; camera/AR chrome is the only deliberate exception)
proposal_seeds: Replace the hard-coded colours on the summary step with PatinaColors dynamic tokens.

title: "Today" reads the same at 7:40am and 9pm
observation: The header is "WEDNESDAY · AUG 26" over the literal word "Today" with a "?" glyph — no greeting, no part-of-day, at any hour.
why_it_matters: The product's thesis is a daily ritual, but the home cannot tell morning coffee from evening couch, so the same card has to serve both moods.
proposal_seeds: Read the TimeOfDay token the design system already ships and let the header name the hour.

title: Two silent fourteen-day decays punish absence
observation: A terminal or matched design request stops being promoted 14 days after its stage anchor, and the Companion mark graduates to its calm "learned" state at 14 days — neither is explained on any screen.
why_it_matters: The returning user's most likely first screen is quieter than the one they left, and nothing tells them why.
already_ruled: C8 (coaching phases and label decay are ruled)
proposal_seeds: Keep a matched designer visible until the relationship actually ends, not on a timer.

title: Return has no instrumentation beyond app_open
observation: The app captures `app_open`, `session_started`, `today_next_move_tapped`, `today_editorial_story_tapped`, `today_active_room_tapped` and `studio_queue_item_activated`, but no push-received, push-opened, notification-permission-outcome or "new since last visit" event exists.
why_it_matters: No decision about return mechanics can be settled with evidence until the trigger-to-open path is measurable.
proposal_seeds: Emit push_received / push_opened / permission_result before shipping any new trigger.

title: Coach-mark bubble hides the element it describes
observation: Tour step 1's bubble ("This is your Daily Room — picks and stories chosen for your space.") is a full-width opaque card that sits directly over the Next Move card it is explaining (g-09) — only the card's trailing arrow icon peeks out past the bubble's edge.
why_it_matters: A teaching moment that occludes its own subject teaches nothing; the user has to dismiss the coach mark before they can see what it was pointing at, breaking the explain-then-look sequence the tour exists for.
proposal_seeds: Position the tour bubble below or beside its anchor with a visible pointer, never on top of it.

title: Filter chips imply catalog-wide scope but only filter one loaded page
observation: Tapping "Seating" changes the subtitle to "3 pieces curated for your space" (g-16), reading as if the catalog holds only 3 seating pieces — the chips filter the same ≤20 rows already on screen; the RPC's `p_category` parameter is never sent.
why_it_matters: A shopper comparing sofas sees a near-empty result (3 items, one of them a blank gradient tile) and reasonably concludes Patina doesn't carry much seating, when the constraint is a client-side filter, not real inventory.
proposal_seeds: Send p_category to get_recommendations on chip tap so counts reflect the real catalog, not the current page.

title: Room stats show undefined abbreviations
observation: The room's stat row reads "0 ITEMS", "— MATCH", "0 IN AR" with no legend anywhere on screen (g-28b, c-24, d-06). "IN AR" never has a value other than 0 for any room, on any account, because no product in the catalog has a usdz model.
why_it_matters: A stat that is permanently 0 and never explained reads as either broken or meaningless the first time it's noticed, and it is always the former — the AR pipeline literally cannot produce a nonzero count today.
proposal_seeds: Drop the "In AR" stat until usdz models exist for at least one product, and label "Match" with what it's matching against.

title: One action is offered under three different names, stacked
observation: The empty room's body copy reads "We've already found pieces that would fit this space. Browse your Daily Room to start building this room.", directly above a button labeled "Browse Picks for This Room", directly above a link labeled "SEE RECOMMENDATIONS →" (g-28b, c-24, d-06) — three different phrasings stacked for what appears to be one underlying destination.
why_it_matters: Three labels for one act make the user pause to work out whether they're different options before tapping any of them — the opposite of the "success looks like" bar T5 sets (piece lands in the room without hunting).
proposal_seeds: Cut to one CTA with one label; drop the body-copy restatement and the redundant link.

title: One screen ignores the dark-mode override entirely
observation: With the system/app appearance set to dark for the whole walk (confirmed by every surrounding shot: d-01, d-02, d-06, d-07, d-08, d-09, d-10 all render dark), the room-summary step "Here's what I see" (d-06a) renders in the app's light theme — cream ground, near-black text — sitting between two dark screens in the same unbroken session.
why_it_matters: A user who set dark mode for eye comfort (bus, night, whatever the reason) gets one jarring bright screen mid-flow with no warning, and it is exactly the screen showing them the corrupted room dimensions (U2-13) — the two defects compound on the same screen.
proposal_seeds: Route the room-summary screen through the same dynamic color tokens as the rest of the room flow.

title: Filters are client-side over twenty rows
observation: Tapping "Seating" changes the subtitle to "3 pieces curated for your space" — the chips filter the twenty rows already fetched rather than sending p_category, and there is no price filter, no sort and no pagination control.
why_it_matters: A shopper who filters to a category sees three pieces and concludes the marketplace is empty, when the catalog simply was not queried.
proposal_seeds: Send p_category to the RPC on chip change and page the results.

title: Saved rows carry no note, room or save date
observation: The only saved row reads "ROOM & BOARD / Heirloom Oak Dining Table / $4200" with a chevron. No room, no date saved, no note, no availability, no price-change marker — and TableItemModel.notes exists with no UI that writes it.
why_it_matters: A saved list that records nothing about why a piece was saved gives a returning shopper no reason to reopen it.
proposal_seeds: Print the room and the save date on each row and let a tap-and-hold add a note.

title: Shipping push exists but never reaches a client order
observation: fulfillment-notify can push "confirmed | in_production | shipped | delivered | eta_change | substitution" to a homeowner's device, but only when an admin operator presses send in the admin portal, and only for fulfillment_orders on the designer-sourced BOH rail — never for direct_orders.
why_it_matters: The exact message that would bring a buyer back after a purchase already exists and is pointed at a rail the client app cannot reach.
proposal_seeds: Point the same templates at direct_orders' fulfillment_status once it exists, and fire on transition rather than on an operator's click.

title: Push routes exist for money that nothing emits
observation: NotificationRouter handles entity types proposal and invoice, and the code states no edge function emits them yet; the patina:// scheme reaches only auth, room and piece, so an emailed or texted link can never open an invoice or a proposal.
why_it_matters: Even when the money notification is finally sent, the tap has nowhere to land unless the deep-link table grows with it.
proposal_seeds: Extend the deep-link hosts to invoice, proposal and order alongside the first money push.

title: No payment marks before the Checkout hand-off
observation: The only statement of how payment works is the caption "Pay securely by card or bank transfer." — no Apple Pay mark, no card marks, no mention that payment opens a Stripe page, and no surcharge preview before the hand-off.
why_it_matters: Apple Pay is already available in the Checkout the app opens, and the client is given no reason to expect the fastest, most trusted way to pay.
proposal_seeds: Show the accepted-method marks under the Pay button and say the payment opens securely in Safari. What would settle this: one device pass with a card in Wallet on a real invoice.

title: No receipts or payment history in the app
observation: The only payments UI is "PAYMENTS / No payments recorded yet."; there is no receipts list, no paid-invoice section on the list ("AWAITING PAYMENT (1)" is the only section), and the settle banner says the receipt "is on its way to your inbox."
why_it_matters: The record of what a household has spent lives in email rather than in the app, removing the most durable reason to keep the app installed after a project ends.
proposal_seeds: Add a paid section to the invoices list and keep every receipt openable in the app.

title: The deposit is for a table the app never shows
observation: "WHAT'S INCLUDED / Dining table — deposit (50%) $2,650.00 / Primary bedroom nightstands (pair) — deposit (50%) $1,600.00". Neither the dining table nor the nightstands appear anywhere else in the app — not on the project, not in a room, not as a piece, not as an order.
why_it_matters: The client pays half the price of a table and then has no object in the app to check on, which is exactly the return visit a furnishing app should own.
proposal_seeds: Link invoice line items to the FF&E selections they pay for and give each one a status the client can open.

title: Saved renders the price as "$4200"
observation: The saved row reads "ROOM & BOARD / Heirloom Oak Dining Table / $4200" while the same piece on the browse grid reads "$4,200".
why_it_matters: The list held up as the record of what someone is saving toward prints money in a format the rest of the app does not use.
proposal_seeds: Route the Saved row through the same currency formatter the grid uses.
Route every price through the one currency formatter the grid already uses.
Route every price through PatinaCurrency.format.

title: Launch screen is blank white, no wordmark
observation: The launch screen is pure blank white — no wordmark, no strata mark, no colour — before the warm cream ground of the app appears. Captured identically on two separate cold launches.
why_it_matters: The one moment the brand owns unconditionally is spent on nothing, and the white flash reads as a broken load.
proposal_seeds: Set the launch storyboard's background to the app's ground colour.
Put the cream ground and the PATINA wordmark on the launch storyboard so the splash and the app agree.

title: "Installation & Styling" truncated to the verb "Install"
observation: The project card shows "PHASE / Install" while the accessibility label carries the full "Installation & Styling"; the project detail one tap away reads "Currently: Installation & Styling". There is no ellipsis, so the phase reads as an instruction.
why_it_matters: The phase name is the designer's own vocabulary and the client's only progress signal, and it is rendered as a command.
proposal_seeds: Let the phase label wrap to two lines instead of truncating without an ellipsis.

title: Launch screen is blank white, no wordmark
observation: Cold launch shows a pure white screen with no logo, no wordmark, no color, for roughly 1.5s before the auth gate — captured identically on two separate cold launches.
why_it_matters: The first thing a client I hand a login to sees is a jarring flash against the app's own warm ground, before anything establishes this is my studio's tool.
proposal_seeds: Render the wordmark on the app's own ground during the splash hold instead of a blank white screen.

title: Companion intro pre-empts first-launch tour step 2
observation: The captured tour shows "Step 1 of 2" (g-09), not the three steps the code declares; the tour's own middle step (anchor .addToRoom, "Save what you love — Add pieces to a room with + Add") has no view to attach to and the Companion intro sequences in ahead of it, so the shipped tour is functionally two steps and the app's save-loop explanation is never spoken.
why_it_matters: The one first-run beat that would have explained how saving/organizing pieces works is silently dropped, which matters for a client who is meant to be building a room with me between meetings, not just browsing.
already_ruled: C8 (11-canon-digest.md §6 correction) — DELIVERY.md names this as an open, unaddressed residual, not settled as delivered.
july_status: residual per DELIVERY.md (not U34's scope)
proposal_seeds: Gate the Companion intro strictly behind FirstLaunchTour completion, or restore a mount point for the .addToRoom anchor.

title: "Sign in" drawn as a circle, label overflowing
observation: The guest empty state's "Sign in" control renders as a circle whose label extends past both edges of the circle.
why_it_matters: The conversion control on the screen that asks a guest to sign in is visibly broken.
proposal_seeds: Use the design kit's capsule button rather than a circular glyph frame.

title: 'Today' never becomes 'good evening'
observation: The header always reads the literal word 'Today,' morning or night. I checked this at the default light-mode time and again in the dark-mode lane's identical layout — same word.
why_it_matters: I check this the way I check the weather — usually at night after the kids are down. A screen that can't tell 9pm from 9am doesn't feel like it's paying attention to my day.
proposal_seeds: Read the existing TimeOfDay token on the home header, the way the Companion's conversation voice already does.

title: Coach-mark buttons use the app's only system blue
observation: "Skip" and "Next"/"Done" render in iOS system blue (#007AFF) on both tour steps (g-09, g-10) — the only blue anywhere in an app whose entire palette is cream/charcoal/mocha/clay.
why_it_matters: The very first interactive controls a new user sees break the brand system before the user has seen anything else to compare it to, undermining the "considered, unhurried" first impression the rest of the screen (Playfair serif, warm tan) is built to give.
proposal_seeds: Style the tour's Skip/Next/Done as PatinaButton .ghost/.secondary, not system-default blue text buttons.

title: Price format changes between the grid and Saved
observation: The same piece prices as "$4,200" on the browse grid and "$4200" (no thousands separator) on its Saved row (g-22b).
why_it_matters: A price that reformats between two screens showing the same number reads as a small crack in an app asking someone to trust a four-figure purchase decision.
proposal_seeds: Route both surfaces through the same currency formatter.

title: The Companion's own headline changes wording for the same panel
observation: The identical "where next" panel is titled "Where to begin?" for a 0-room guest (g-14b) and "Where to next?" for a 1-room activeProject client (d-09, x-09) — two headlines for what is functionally the same menu of Companion rows.
why_it_matters: Minor on its own, but it's one more instance of the app not having a single stable name for a recurring piece of UI — the same pattern this program's grounding already flags for the designer-help CTA and the taste-portrait label; small inconsistencies like this compound into an app that reads as less considered than its visual design promises.
proposal_seeds: This one may be intentional (0 rooms vs. 1+ rooms) — worth a ruling either way rather than an unreviewed drift.

title: Marketplace copy says "curated"
observation: The Browse header subtitle reads "10 pieces curated for your space" (and "curated for this room" when scoped).
why_it_matters: The brand voice rules the deck is written against name "curated" as marketplace haze to avoid, on the one screen where the app is asking to be trusted with money.
already_ruled: C6
proposal_seeds: Rewrite the subtitle in plain Midwest English, e.g. "10 pieces chosen for this room".
